621.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). All beings and creatures are of his making; he alone is the helper of the Sants. He himself keeps (the honour) of his servant, and (the servant's) glory has become complete. The perfect Supreme Lord is with me. The Perfect Guru has kept (my honour) wholly, and all have become kind (to me). Nanak meditates night and day on the Naam (of him who is) the Giver of soul and breath of life. He keeps his servant held close to his breast, as a father and mother (hold) a child. ॥2॥
621.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 3, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Meeting the village headmen, I was not rid of (my) anxiety; from the chiefs I got no reassurance; (I laid my) dispute before the nobles (too); (but only) on meeting Ram, the King, was it settled. Now I go nowhere searching, for I have met Gobind, the Guru, the Lord of the earth. When I came to God's court, then all (my) outcry was stilled. I have found what was mine to find; then where is there to come, and where to go? There, matters are settled by true justice; there, master and servant are equal. The Knower of hearts knows (all); he himself understands without a word being spoken. He is the King of every place; there the unstruck Shabad resounds. What cleverness (can work) before him? O Nanak, shed self-conceit and meet him. ॥4॥
621.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Enshrine the Naam in (your) heart; meditate on the Guru while sitting at home. The Perfect Guru has declared the Truth; (through it) that true peace has been found. (Our) own Guru has become merciful; having bathed, (we) have come home with bliss, peace, well-being and joy. The Guru's greatness is true and lasting; its worth cannot be told. (The Guru is) the Emperor above the heads of kings. On meeting the Guru, the mind fills with eager joy. All sins have been shed, by joining with the Saadh Sangat. The Lord's Name is a treasure of virtues; repeating it, (all) tasks have been fulfilled. The Guru has opened up the door of liberation; all creation hails him. O Nanak, God is with me; the fears of birth and death have left (me). ॥4॥
621.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Perfect Guru has shown grace, and God has fulfilled our longing. Having bathed, (we) have come home, and have found bliss, joy and peace. O Sants, through the Name of Ram one is carried across. Rising and sitting, let us meditate on the Lord, Har Har, and do good deeds night and day. The Sant's path is the ladder of righteousness; only some fortunate one finds it. The sins of millions of births are gone for one who fixes his mind on the Lord's feet. Ever praise your own God, who has kept his full power (at work in all); all beings and creatures have been made pure, through the True Guru's teaching of the Truth. Destroyer of obstacles, dispeller of all sorrows: such is the Naam the True Guru has made firm (within); sins are cast off, all have become pure, and servant Nanak has come home in peace. ॥4॥
622.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (You are) the Master, fathomless in virtues; (my) home and household, all are yours. O Guru, O Gopal, you are (my) protector; all beings have become kind (to me). I abide in bliss, meditating on the Guru's feet; in God's refuge, fear comes from no quarter. O Murari, you (dwell) in the hearts of your servants; God has raised (in them) a foundation that never shakes. Your support is (my) strength and wealth; you are my mighty Master. All who have found the Saadh Sangat, God himself has carried across. In his grace (God) has given the sweet essence of the Naam, and all is well and at peace. God has become (my) helper; all (the world) has risen and fallen at (my) feet. Let us meditate on God with every breath; O Nanak, let us sing the Lord's song of joy. ॥4॥
622.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Peace, Sahaj and bliss (have come); God, dear to (my) mind, has met (me). The Perfect Guru showed grace, and then came my liberation. (My) mind is absorbed in loving devotion to the Lord, and (within) the unstruck vina plays always. The shelter of the Lord's feet is strong; all dependence on people has ended. The Life of the world, the Giver, has been found, and (I) have sung the Lord's virtues, relishing (his love) again and again. God has cut the noose of Jam; the mind's hope is fulfilled. Wherever I look, there he is; there is none but the Lord God. In his grace God has protected (us); all the sorrows of birth after birth are gone. (I) have meditated on the Naam of the Fearless One, and Nanak has found unshakeable peace. ॥4॥
622.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Creator has brought calm; the fever has left the family. The Perfect Guru has protected (us), (when we) looked to the refuge of the True One. The Supreme God himself has become the protector; in a moment calm, Sahaj and peace sprang up, and the mind is at ease for ever. (He) has given the medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har; it has rooted out all the disease. (He) showed his own grace, and he has set every matter right. God has kept to his own age-old way (of grace); (he) has not weighed our merits and faults. The Guru's Shabad has become manifest; it has kept all (our) honour. I speak what you have me speak; You are the Master, fathomless in virtues. Repeat the Naam, O Nanak: it is the true witness; (God) has kept the honour of his own servant. ॥4॥
623.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Creator, the all-pervading Being, himself stood in the midst, and not a hair was harmed. The Guru brought the bathing to fruition; repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, sins have been destroyed. O Sants, the pool of Ramdas is beautiful; whoever bathes (in it) carries his family across, and his own soul is set free. The world sings (his) acclaim, (and) he obtains the fruits his mind longs for. (We) have bathed and come (back) safe and sound, and have meditated on (our) own God. Whoever bathes in the pool of the Sants reaches the supreme state. He neither dies nor comes and goes, meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Only he understands this reflection on God on whom God, the Lord, is merciful. O brother, Nanak (has come) to God's refuge, which has wiped out all worry and anxious reckoning. ॥4॥
The pool of Ramdas (Ramdas Sarovar): the sacred pool at Amritsar, begun by Guru Ram Das Ji and named after him; Ramdas also means the servants of Ram, so the pool is read too as the Saadh Sangat.
623.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme Lord has seen (his love for his servant) through in full; nothing at all has been left wanting. Attaching (his servants) to (his) feet, the Guru has carried (them) across; (they) cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har. (God) is ever the protector of his own servant; in his grace he has made (them) his own and kept them, and reared (them) as a mother and father would. The fortunate have found the True Guru, who has wiped out the road of Jam. (Their) minds are set on the Lord's devotion and love; repeating (the Name) they live, those fortunate ones. (The Lord's servant) sings the Lord's Amrit Bani, and bathes in the dust of the Saadhs' feet. (God) himself has given his own Name; God the Creator has saved (him). The sight of the Lord is the support of (his) breath of life; this is (his) complete and pure understanding. Show grace, O Knower of hearts: servant Nanak is in your refuge, O Master. ॥4॥
623.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Perfect Guru has joined (us) to (the Lord's) feet, and (we) have found the Lord, ever with (us), our helper. Wherever we go, there we are at ease; in his grace, God has united (us with himself). Sing the Lord's praises always, with love; you will obtain every fruit the mind longs for, and (the Lord will be) a helper at the side of your soul. Narayan is the support of (my) breath of life; I am the dust of the Sants' feet. (These Sants) have made the fallen pure; in their grace, they have given (them) the Lord's praise. The Supreme Lord cherishes (them), ever beside the soul as its protector. Let us sing the Lord's Kirtan day and night; (then) one is not cast into births again. The one to whom the all-pervading Being, the Creator, gives (this gift): that one alone has known the Lord's sweet essence. Jam's servant has not come near (him); O Nanak, (he) has found peace in (God's) refuge. ॥4॥
624.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Perfect Guru has brought everything to fulfilment; God pervades all, filling every place. The bathing has taken place in peace and well-being; I am a sacrifice to the Supreme Lord. With the Guru's lotus feet enshrined in the heart, not the least hindrance befalls; all (my) affairs have been set right. Meeting the Saadh (the Guru), (people) have shed their evil-mindedness; the fallen have all become pure. Those who have bathed in the pool of Ramdas: all the sins they committed have been washed off. Let us sing Gobind's praises every day, and, joining the Saadh Sangat, meditate (on him). That one obtains the fruits the mind desires who meditates on the Perfect Guru in the heart. The great Gopal is bliss itself; repeating again and again (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss, one lives. Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam; God has kept to his own age-old way. ॥4॥
624.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In all ten directions the clouds spread like a canopy, bank upon bank; the lightning flashes and frightens (me). (My) bed is lonely, there is no sleep in (my) eyes: (my) Husband has gone away to a far land. Now no message (from him) comes, O mother. (Once,) when my Beloved travelled even one kos, four letters would reach (me). How could this dear Beloved be forgotten, who has every virtue and gives every comfort? Climbing up to the rooftop, I watch the road (for him), and my eyes have filled with tears. The wall of ego, of I and I, has risen between (us); I hear that he is near, in (my own) land. The screen (between us) is (as thin as) a butterfly's wing, yet, unseen, he seems far away. The Master of all became merciful and wiped away all (my) pain. Says Nanak, the Guru knocked down the wall of Haumai, and then (I) found Bithal, the Merciful. All (my) anxiety is gone, O mother; the Guru has brought (me) to the one I longed for: the King, the treasure of every virtue. ॥11॥
Bithal (Vitthal): a name of God, the One who stands beyond Maya.
Rahao Dooja: the second Rahao (Pause) of this shabad; in it the longing of the first Rahao is fulfilled.
624.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord, you are) the Restorer of what was lost, the Releaser of captives, the Formless One, the Healer of pain. I know nothing of good deeds, nothing of Dharma; I am greedy, clinging to Maya. (Yet) I have come to be called Govind's devotee: keep this honour, which is yours. Dear Lord, you are the honour of those without honour; my Govind makes the worthless precious; I am a sacrifice to your might. Just as a child, out of fondness and its own nature, commits a hundred thousand faults, and the father, teaching it, scolds it in many ways, and then holds it close again, (so) God forgives past failings and sets (one) on the path for what lies ahead. The Lord, the Knower of hearts, knows every state; to whom else, then, should one tell it? Gobind is not won over by mere talk and telling; if it pleases the Lord, (one's) honour is kept. I have looked at every other shelter; yours is the one shelter I keep. God the Master, kind and merciful, himself hears the prayer, brings (one) to meet the Perfect True Guru, and all the mind's anxiety ends. The medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has been put into (my) mouth; servant Nanak dwells in peace. ॥4॥
625.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering God over and over, (we) have come into bliss; all pain and strife have fled. Singing the praises of our God and meditating on him, all (our) affairs have been set in order. (O God,) your Name is the life of all the world. From the Perfect Guru (we) received the teaching; repeating (the Name), (we) have been carried across the terrifying world-ocean. You alone are (your own) counsellor, O God, and you hear (all); you alone are able to do all things. It is you who give and you who enjoy; of what account is this poor creature? What virtues of yours could I speak of and describe? Your worth cannot be told. Beholding his God again and again, (one) lives; wondrous is your greatness. O God, my Master, showing your favour, you yourself have made (my) honour and understanding whole. Nanak is a sacrifice for ever and ever; I long for the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
625.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Whoever) bows to the Perfect Guru: God has set right all (his) affairs. The Lord has shown his grace; God has fully upheld (his) honour. (God) has become the helper of his servant; the Creator has fulfilled every wish; nothing is left wanting. The Creator, the all-pervading Being, has had the pool made; Maya has followed along behind; there is no shortage anywhere. So it pleases my Perfect True Guru. Remembering the Merciful One again and again, all beings have become kind (to me). All acclaim to the Lord of the world, who has made the whole design complete. You are my great Master; this treasure is your own gift. Servant Nanak has meditated on the One, and has received the blessing that bears every fruit. ॥4॥
625.3: Raag Sorath, Ghar 3, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those who have bathed in the pool of Ramdas: all the sins they committed have been washed away; bathing, they have become pure; this is the gift of the Perfect Guru. God has bestowed all peace and well-being; everything has been kept safe and sound, by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. In the Saadh Sangat the filth (of the mind) has been washed off; the Supreme Lord has become (our) companion. Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and has found God, the Primal Being. ॥2॥
625.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The (house of the heart) in which the Supreme Lord has come to mind: that house the Master has made to flourish. When (one) found the Guru, the Ocean of peace, then (he) wiped out all doubt. The glory of the Lord's Name, the singing of (his) praises at all hours: (this gift I) have received from the Perfect Guru. The story of God is beyond telling; his servants speak the Bani that is Amrit. Servant Nanak has uttered (it), having come to know (it) through the Perfect Guru. ॥2॥
626.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ahead, (in the world beyond,) the Guru has given peace; behind, (in this world,) too, the Guru has brought peace and well-being. (I) have found all treasures and comforts, (for I) have meditated on my Guru in (my) heart. (Such is) the greatness of my own True Guru: (through him) one obtains the fruits the mind longs for; O Sants, (this greatness) grows more and more, day by day. All beings and creatures have become kind (to me); God has made (them) his own. Gopal has been met, naturally, in Sahaj; O Nanak, (they) have found contentment in the True One. ॥2॥
626.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru's Shabad is (our) protector, a watch kept all around us. The mind is fixed on the Name of Ram; Jam has fled in shame. Dear God, it is you who give me peace; cutting away the bonds (of Maya), the perfect, all-pervading Being, the Creator, makes the mind pure. O Nanak, God is imperishable; service done to him will not go in vain. Your servants revel in bliss; repeating (your Name), (their) hope has been fulfilled. ॥2॥
626.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has fully upheld (my) honour. (I) have found the fruit the mind longed for, (for I) have always meditated on my God. O Sants, without him there is no other; that God alone is the Cause of creation. My own God has granted blessings, and has brought all beings under (his) sway. Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and so (he) has wiped out all (his) sorrows. ॥2॥
626.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The perfect Guru has taken away the fever; the unstruck trumpets play. God has brought about every blessing; he himself has given them, out of his mercy. The True Guru himself has taken away the pain; all the Sikhs and Sants, meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have become full of joy. Whatever (your Sants) ask for, they receive; O God, you (yourself) give to your own Sants. God has saved Hargobind; servant Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the True One. ॥2॥
626.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) have (me) do only what pleases you; I have no cleverness at all. We, (your) children, are in your refuge; God himself has kept (our) honour. O Lord King, (you are) my mother and father; in your mercy you have taken (me) into your care; I do what you have me do. All beings and creatures are upheld by you; O God, (their) string is in your hands. whatever he has (us) do, that alone is done; servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥2॥
627.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord's Name has been threaded into the heart, (and so) all our work has been done. The mind of that one has become attached to God's feet whose fortune is full. Joining the Saadh Sangat, (I) have meditated on the Lord; at all hours (I) have worshipped the Lord, Har Har, and have found the fruit the mind longed for. The shoot (of deeds) from lives long past has sprung up, (and) the mind has become attached to the Name of Ram. Staying absorbed, in mind and body, in the sight of the Lord, servant Nanak sings the praises of the True One. ॥2॥
627.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Whoever), meeting the Guru, has remembered God has set all (his) affairs right. No one speaks ill (of him); all the world acclaims (him). O Sants, the Master's refuge is the one that stands for ever; all beings and creatures are in his hands alone; that God is the Knower of hearts. (God) has set right all (his) works; God has kept to his own age-old way (of grace). God's Name purifies the fallen; servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to it). ॥2॥
627.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme Lord fashioned (this child) and made (him) fair; the Guru has saved this little one. Let father and mother rejoice; the Supreme God is the giver of life. Your servants wish (all) well, (O Lord); you keep the honour of your servant, and set (his) affairs right yourself. My God does good to others, he who has set his full power (in all creation). Nanak has come to (his) refuge, and has found the fruit the mind longed for. ॥2॥
627.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeat (the Name of) the Lord for ever and ever; God himself is the protector of children. (He) has held back the smallpox; through the Lord's praise the dangers have gone. My God has ever been merciful; he has heard the prayer of his devotee, and has become kind to all beings. God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful; remembering the Lord, all pain has gone. (He) has heard the plea of his servant; O Nanak, all the world sleeps in peace. ॥2॥
Sitala is smallpox, which people took to be the wrath of the goddess Sitala.
627.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meditating on our own Guru, (and) meeting (him), (we) have come home safe and well. (This is) the glory of the Naam; its worth cannot be told. O Sants, worship the Lord, Har, Har, Har; worshipping the Lord, everything is obtained: (so) bring all (your) tasks to fulfilment. Loving devotion to God has taken hold (of the mind); only that one receives (this gift) whose fortune is great. O servant Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam has found the fruit that gives every comfort. ॥2॥
627.6: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme God has raised a dam (against misfortune), (and) has broken up the camp of pain and disease. Men and women rejoice; God, the Lord, Har Har, has shown mercy. O Sants, there is peace everywhere; the Supreme Lord, the perfect Supreme God, pervades every place. The Bani has come from God, the very source; it has wiped away all anxiety. The merciful Being has been kind; Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the Lord, the True One. ॥2॥
628.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Here and hereafter (he is) the protector: God, the True Guru, merciful to the meek. He himself protects his servants; in every heart (it is he who) speaks the word. I offer myself as a sacrifice at the Guru's feet; day and night, with every breath, I keep in mind (God), who pervades all places. (God) himself has become (my) helper; true is the gift of the True One. Devotion to you and your praise Nanak has found in your refuge, O God. ॥2॥
628.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When it pleased the perfect True Guru, then (I) repeated the Name of Ram. Gobind showed mercy, (and) God kept our honour. The Lord's feet ever give peace; whatever (those who hold to them) wish for, that very fruit they receive; (their) hope does not go empty. The one on whom the Lord of life, the Giver, shows mercy: that Sant alone sings (his) praises. his mind is absorbed in loving devotion, and he is pleasing to the mind of the Supreme Lord. With the Lord's praise uttered at all hours, the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures has worn off. My Creator has united (me) with himself; the Sants, the holy ones, have become (my) companions. He has taken (me) by the hand, given (me) all things, and himself joined (me) to himself. Says Nanak, every undertaking has been fulfilled: (I) have found the perfect True Guru. ॥4॥
628.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Humility is our mace; (to be) the dust and ashes beneath the feet of all is (our) double-edged sword. Before this no evildoer can stand; the perfect Guru has taught this. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the shelter of the Sants; whoever remembers it is set free, and millions upon millions are saved. In the company of the Sants (I) have sung (his) praise, (and) have found this perfect wealth of the Lord. Says Nanak, (I) have erased self-conceit, (and) everywhere the Supreme Lord has come into view. ॥2॥
628.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The perfect Guru has shown (his) full (grace), (and) has bestowed his own gift. (I) have found lasting bliss and peace; (he) has made every place dwell in peace. Devotion to the Lord gives (every) fruit; the perfect Guru in his mercy has given it; only some rare one has known it. Let us sing Gurbani, O brother; it ever bears fruit and gives peace. O Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam has received what was written for him beforehand. ॥2॥
628.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Worshipping the perfect Guru, (I) have accomplished all (my) tasks; all (my) wishes are fulfilled, (and) the unstruck trumpets play. O Sants, repeating (the Name of) Ram, (I) have found peace; (I) have come to dwell in the abode of the Sants in peace and Sahaj, and have wiped away all sorrows. The Bani of the perfect Guru is pleasing to the mind of the Supreme Lord. Servant Nanak has uttered it: (it is) the pure story of the One beyond words. ॥2॥
629.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). A hungry man feels no shame in eating; just so does the Lord's servant sing the Lord's praises. Why be slack about our own task, the remembrance through which the face is bright in the Lord's court, and peace is found for ever and ever? As the lustful man is lured by lust, so the Lord's praise is dear to the Lord's servant. As a mother clings to her child, so the one who knows (God) practises the Naam. (The one who) receives (this gift) from the perfect Guru, O servant Nanak, (he alone) meditates on the Naam. ॥4॥
629.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (I) have come home in peace and well-being; ash has fallen on the slanderer's face. The Perfect Guru has robed (me) in honour, and all (my) sorrows have perished. O Sants, this is the greatness of the True One, who has brought about a wondrous glory. (He) speaks as the Master wills: the servant utters the Bani and proclaims God. O Nanak, God is the Giver of peace, who has made a perfect arrangement. ॥2॥
629.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meditating on our own God in the heart, (we) have come home safe and sound. Contentment has come about in the world; the Perfect Guru has taken hold of (us) and carried (us) across. O Sants, my God is ever merciful. He does not count up the account of his devotee; Gopal protects his children. Whoever keeps the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart has set all things in order. The Perfect Guru, pleased, has given (the gift of the Name); since then, O Nanak, there has been no sorrow. ॥2॥
629.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That same Lord has come to dwell in (my) mind and body; everyone hails (me) in triumph. This is the greatness of the Perfect Guru; its worth cannot be told. I am a sacrifice to your Name. O my Beloved, the one whom you forgive sings your praise. You are my great Master; the Sants put their trust in you. O God, Nanak has come to your refuge; ash is on the slanderer's face. ॥2॥
629.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ahead, in the world to come, there is peace, my friend, and behind, in this world, bliss: God has brought it about. The Supreme God has made such an arrangement that (I) waver no more, anywhere. (My) mind has come to trust the True Master; (I) have known the Lord to be in all, through and through. All beings are yours, O Merciful One; you sustain your own devotees. Your greatness is a wonder; Nanak meditates on the Naam every day. ॥2॥
630.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Narayan is with me; Death's messenger does not come near (me). Holding (me) close to his bosom, God protects (me): (this is) owing to the True Guru's teaching of the Truth. The Perfect Guru has made all complete: he has struck down and routed all the enemies, and given his servant good understanding. God has made all the places flourish; (we) have come back in peace and well-being. Nanak has come to the refuge of God, who has wiped away all diseases. ॥2॥
630.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The True Guru is the Giver of all comforts; let us fall into his refuge. On receiving the sight of him bliss arises and sorrow has gone; let us sing of the Lord. Drink the Lord's sweet essence, O brother; repeat the Naam, worship the Naam alone, in the refuge of the Perfect Guru. It comes to him alone for whom it is written from the start; he alone is perfect, O brother. Dear God, this is Nanak's prayer: that I may stay with my mind attuned to the Naam. ॥2॥
630.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, who does and causes all to be done, the Knower of hearts, keeps (the honour) of his own servant; (that servant) is hailed throughout the world, and tastes the sweet essence of the Guru's Shabad. Dear God, O Lord of the world, I have your shelter. You are all-powerful, the Giver of refuge; at all hours I meditate on you. O God, the servant who worships you has no anxiety; touching the True Guru's feet, his fear is wiped away, and he has sung the Lord's praises in his mind. O True Guru, those you have comforted (have) peace, Sahaj and bliss in plenty; victorious, they have come home with honour, and their hope is fulfilled. The Guru is perfect, and perfect is his teaching; the works of God are perfect. Clinging to the Guru's feet and repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Nanak has crossed the world-ocean. ॥4॥
630.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The destroyer of the pains of the poor has become merciful; he himself has arranged everything. He has saved his own servant in an instant; the Perfect Guru has cut through (his) fetters. O my mind, let us always meditate on the Guru, Govind; all troubles are wiped from this body, and one obtains the fruit the mind longs for. The God by whom all beings and creatures were made is lofty, beyond reach, without limit. In the Saadh Sangat Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and (his) face is radiant in the Lord's court. ॥2॥
630.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I remember my own Master; day and night I meditate on him always, who has given his hand and saved (his servants); they have tasted the Lord's Name, the supreme sweet essence. (I am) a sacrifice to my own Guru: the perfect God, the Giver, has become merciful, and (all) beings have become kind (to me). Servant Nanak has come to the refuge of the One who has kept (his) honour in full and wiped away all (his) sorrows. Enjoy peace, O my brothers. ॥2॥
631.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hear (my) prayer, O my Master: all beings and creatures are upheld by you. Keep the honour of your own Name, O you who do and cause all to be done. Dear God, my Beloved, do a Master's part by (us): bad or good, we are yours. The almighty Master has heard the plea; cutting away (their) bonds, he has made (them) fair. Dressing his servants in robes of honour, he has joined them (to himself); O Nanak, they have become known throughout the world. ॥2॥
631.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) has made all beings and creatures subject (to his servants), and all (his) servants (are honoured) at (his) court. God has taken his own as his own, and carried them across the world-ocean. He has set right all the affairs of the Sants, our perfect Master, merciful to the meek, kind, the treasure of mercy. Bidden come and sit, (they are) honoured everywhere, and lack nothing in any way. He has given his servants the robe of honour of devotion; O Nanak, God's glory has become known. ॥2॥
631.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, give your love to Ram; let your ears hear Gobind's praises, and your tongue sing (his) songs. Join the Saadh Sangat and remember Madho; (so) the fallen become pure. Death roams like a snake, its jaws spread wide, my friend. Today or tomorrow it will swallow you too; grasp this and hold it in your mind. Says Nanak: worship Ram; the moment is passing. ॥2॥
631.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). The mind's longing has stayed within the mind itself: (he) neither worshipped the Lord nor served the holy, who are the true tiraths, and Death has seized (him) by the hair. Wife, friends, sons, chariots, property, wealth, the whole earth entire: know these and all else to be false; only the worship of Ram is real. Wandering on and on through many ages you grew weary, and (now) you have gained the human body. Says Nanak: this is your turn to meet (him); why do you not remember (him)? ॥2॥
Tirath: here the holy, who are themselves the true places of pilgrimage; the like line of the next shabad has gur janu, the Guru, in its place.
631.5: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mind, what evil understanding have you taken up? You are wrapped up in the relish of other men's wives and of slander, and have not practised devotion to Ram. You have not known the path of liberation, and have run about to amass wealth. In the end no one has kept (anyone) company; you have had yourself bound for nothing. You have neither worshipped the Lord nor served the Guru, and no wisdom at all has welled up (in you). The Stainless One is right within your own heart, and you search the wilderness (for him). Wandering through many births you have grown weary, yet have not gained a steady understanding. Having gained the station of the human body, worship the Lord: this is the counsel Nanak has given. ॥3॥
632.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mind, reflect upon the refuge of God; Ganika was saved by remembering him: keep his praise enshrined in your heart. By remembering him Dhru became immovable and reached the fearless state; such a Master, the remover of sorrow: why have you forgotten him? The moment he took the shelter of the treasure of mercy, Gaj, the elephant, was freed from the crocodile. How far can I tell the glory of the Name? As he uttered Ram, his bond was broken. The world knows Ajamal as a sinner; in the twinkling of an eye he was carried across. Says Nanak: remember (God), the wish-fulfilling jewel, and you too will cross over. ॥3॥

Ganika: a courtesan, saved by teaching a parrot to say Ram. Dhru: the child prince who, slighted by his stepmother, gave himself to devotion and was given an unmoving place as the Pole Star. Gaj: in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free. Ajamal: a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called on his son Narayan.
632.2: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). What means should a mortal take up, by which he may gain devotion to Ram and shake off the dread of Jam? Tell me: what deeds, what sort of learning, and then what dharma should he practise? Which Name is it, O Guru, by remembering which one may cross the world-ocean? In Kalyug the Name of the treasure of mercy is the one (way); whoever repeats it attains liberation. No other dharma equals it; so the Veda declares. He whom (people) call the Lord of the world is beyond pleasure and pain, ever untouched; O Nanak, he dwells within you yourself, through and through, like (a reflection) in a mirror. ॥3॥
632.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mother, how am I to recognise the Lord of the world? My mind remains entangled in great attachment, in the darkness of ignorance. I have wasted my whole life wandering in doubt upon doubt, and have not gained a steady understanding. Night and day I have stayed attached to the pleasures of the senses, and (my) baseness has not left me. I have never kept the Saadh Sangat, nor sung the praises of God. In me, servant Nanak, there is no virtue at all; keep me safe in your refuge. ॥2॥
632.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mother, my mind is not in my power. Night and day it runs after the pleasures of the senses; by what means am I to hold it back? It hears the teachings of the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, yet does not let them dwell in the heart for a single moment; absorbed in others' wealth and others' wives, it passes its life in vain. In the intoxication of Maya it has gone mad; it has no inkling of wisdom at all. The Stainless One dwells within the heart itself, (yet) it has not known his secret. As soon as it came to the refuge of the Saadh, all (its) evil understanding was destroyed; then, O Nanak, it remembered (God), the wish-fulfilling jewel, and the noose of Jam was cut. ॥3॥
633.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O man, hold this truth fast in your heart: the whole world is like a dream; it takes no time at all to perish. A wall of sand, though raised and plastered with care, does not last four days; just so are these pleasures of Maya; you fool, why are you caught up (in them)? Understand even now, nothing is lost yet; worship the Name of Murari. Says Nanak: I have proclaimed to you aloud the Saadhs' own counsel. ॥2॥
633.2: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). In this world (I) have seen no friend at all. The whole world is bent on its own comfort; in sorrow (no one) stands by. Wife, friends, sons and kin are all attached to wealth; the moment they saw the man penniless, they all left his company and fled. What am I to say to this crazed mind? It has given its love to these, and the praise of the Master of the meek, who dispels every fear, it has forgotten. Like a dog's tail, (it) has not become straight, though I have tried hard. Says Nanak: (O God,) keep the honour of your age-old way; I have taken your Name. ॥3॥
633.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mind, you have not taken up the Guru's teaching. What of it, if you have shaved your head and put on saffron robes? Leaving the True, (man) has clung to the false, and lost his life to no purpose; by deceit he has fed his own belly, and slept like a beast. He has not known the way of Ram's worship, and has sold himself into Maya's hands; the madman has stayed entangled in the pleasures of the senses, and forgotten the jewel of the Naam. He has stayed heedless, not remembered Gobind, and his span of life has run out in vain. Says Nanak: O Lord, keep in mind your age-old way; mortals are forever going astray. ॥3॥
633.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). The man who in sorrow does not feel sorrow, who has no fondness for pleasure and no fear, who holds gold as clay; in whom there is neither slander nor praise, nor greed, attachment and pride; who stays aloof from joy and grief, (for whom) there is neither honour nor dishonour; who gives up all hope and desire, and expects nothing of the world; whom lust and anger do not touch: in his heart Brahm (God) dwells. The man on whom the Guru has shown grace has recognised this way; O Nanak, he has merged with Gobind as water merges with water. ॥3॥
634.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Know this in your mind, dear friend: the world is bound up in its own comfort alone; no one belongs to anyone. In good times many come and sit together (with one), and keep (him) surrounded on all four sides; when hardship falls, all of them leave his company, and no one comes near. The wife of the house, so dearly loved, who always stays close at his side, the moment the swan (the soul) left this body, fled from him, crying, pret, pret (a ghost). Such are the dealings of those to whom (one) has given his love; at the last moment, O Nanak, no one but the dear Lord has been of any use. ॥3॥
634.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis Chautuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I do not fall into duality, I worship none but the Lord, I go to no tomb or cremation ground. Caught up in craving, I do not go to another's house; the Naam has quenched (my) craving. Within the home (of the heart) the Guru has shown (God's) home; it is pleasing to (my) mind, dyed in Sahaj. You yourself are the Knower, you yourself the Discerner; it is you who give understanding, O Master. Dyed in bairag (longing for the Lord), the mind has become a bairagi (detached from the world); my mind is pierced by the Shabad, O my mother. Within is (God's) Light, the Bani through and through, and the mind is attuned to the True Master. Countless bairagis talk of bairag, (but) he is the bairagi who pleases the Master; (who), through the Shabad, is steeped in his heart in (God's) fear always, and does the Guru's work; (who) remembers the One alone, whose mind does not waver, (who) checks it as it runs and holds it still; (who), rapt in Sahaj, ever dyed in (God's) love, sings the praises of the True One. If the mind, (restless as) the wind, dwells even a little in the Name, the home of peace, there is peace, O brother; (his) tongue, eyes and ears are dyed in the True One; the burning (of craving) is put out: (O God,) it is you who have put it out. The bairagi stays free of hopes, and sits in deep absorption in his own home (within). Sated with the alms of the Naam, (such ones) are content; in Sahaj they have been given Amrit to drink. In duality there is no bairag, so long as there is even a mustard-seed of other (hope). The whole world is yours, you are the one Giver; there is no other, none second, O dear one. Manmukh creatures dwell in sorrow always; to the Gurmukh (God) gives glory. (He) is limitless, without end, unreachable, beyond the senses; (his) worth is not found by telling. (He) abides in Sunn Samadhi, the Lord of the three worlds; (his) Name is the highest good of all. On the foreheads of beings born into the world is a writ; each one bears the writ upon his own head. (God) himself has (beings) do their deeds and good deeds; he himself makes devotion firm (in them). By heeding (God's) fear, the filth of mind and mouth is removed; the Unreachable One himself (grants) wisdom. Only those who have tasted (it) know its flavour, like the sweet a mute has eaten. What can be said of the Indescribable, O brother? May I walk ever in (his) Will. If the Guru unites (one) with the Giver, then understanding comes; one without a Guru has no understanding at all. As he makes us walk, so we walk, O brother; what other cleverness can anyone try? Some are led astray in doubt, some are dyed in devotion; your play is boundless. Whatever you have set (beings) to, such fruit (they) have received; you are the One who moves (all) by your Hukam. Had I something that was mine, I would serve (you) with it; this soul and body are yours. On meeting the True Guru, grace has been shown, and the Amrit Name is (my) support. He who dwells in the inner sky (the highest spiritual realm): in him virtues shine forth, and in virtues are (his) wisdom and meditation. The Naam is pleasing to (his) mind; he utters it and has (others) utter it, and tells of the Essence of essences alone. The Shabad of the Guru, the Pir, is deep and profound; without the Shabad the world has gone mad. O Nanak, the one whose mind accepts the True One is the perfect bairagi, blessed with good fortune, (abiding) in Sahaj. ॥8॥
Sunn Samadhi: absorption in Sunn, the stillness where no worldly thought stirs.
Bhai: in the lines that speak to God as you, it is a loving address to him, O dear one; in the other lines, O brother.
635.1: Raag Sorath, a Tituki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Hopes and desires are bonds, O brother, and religious rites bring bondage; through sin and merit the world is born, O brother, and forgetting the Naam it perishes; this Maya bewitches the world, O brother, and all (such) rites are vain. Listen, O pandit, you who perform rites: the deed from which peace springs, O brother, is reflection on the essence of the self. (The pandit) stands up and recites the Shastra and the Veda, O brother, (but) the deeds you do are worldly; by hypocrisy the filth does not go, O brother; within is the filth of vice. In this way the spider perishes, O brother, hanging head down (in its own web). Through evil understanding many have been ruined, O brother, led astray by the love of another. Without the True Guru the Naam is not found, O brother, and without the Naam doubt does not go. If (one) serves the True Guru, then he finds peace, O brother, and his coming and going ends. Lasting Sahaj springs from the Guru, O brother, and the mind, made pure, merges in the True One. He who serves the Guru understands, O brother; without the Guru the path is not found. What do rites avail the one within whom is greed, O brother? Speaking falsehood, he eats poison. O pandit, when curd is churned, O brother, the essence (butter) comes out of it; churn water, and water is all one sees, O brother; this world is just such a thing. Without the Guru one is ruined in doubt, O brother, (though) the unseen Lord is in every heart. This world is a thread of cotton yarn, O brother, tied by Maya in all ten directions; without the Guru the knot is not untied, O brother; (people) have grown weary performing rites. This world is led astray by doubt, O brother; nothing can be said (of it). On meeting the Guru, the fear (of God) dwells in the mind, O brother; to die in (that) fear is the true writ. Bathing (at tiraths), charity, good deeds: (yet) in the Lord's court the Naam excels, O brother. The Guru is the goad (that drives the elephant), who has made the Naam firm (within), O brother; (the Naam) has come to dwell in the mind, and the outward garb is gone. This body is the Assayer's shop, O brother, and the merchandise is the infinite Naam. That trader secures this merchandise, O brother, who reflects through the Guru's Shabad. Blessed, O Nanak, is the trader, O brother, who carries on (this) trade in the company (of the holy). ॥8॥
636.1: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who have served the True Guru, beloved: their companions (too) have crossed over. No bar is put in their way, beloved; on (their) tongue is the Lord's Amrit. Without (God's) fear, those heavy (with sins) have drowned, beloved; (God) carries (one) across when he casts his glance of grace. Ever you alone are to be praised, O Beloved; ever, your praise (is to be sung). Without the ship (of this praise) one drowns in the fearful (ocean), Beloved; where is the shore to be reached? The Praiseworthy One is to be praised, beloved; there is no other, none second. Those who praise my God are good, beloved; those dyed in the Shabad are coloured with (his) love. If one gains the company of such a one, beloved, he tastes the sweet essence and, churning, (reaches) the Essence (God). Honour is the pass of the True One, beloved, and the Naam is (its) true seal. Whoever has come must write (this pass) and take it along, beloved; recognise the Hukam of the One who commands. Without the Guru the Hukam is not understood, beloved; the True One's might stands for ever. By the Hukam (a being) is conceived, beloved; by the Hukam (it grows) within the womb; by the Hukam it is born, beloved, upside down, head first. The Gurmukh is known in the Lord's court, beloved; he departs having set his task right. By the Hukam (a being) has come, beloved; by the Hukam alone he departs. By the Hukam he is bound and driven off, beloved; the manmukh receives punishment. By the Hukam (God) is recognised through the Shabad, beloved, and (one) goes to the Lord's court robed in honour. By the Hukam accounts are reckoned, beloved; by the Hukam are Haumai and duality. By the Hukam (a being) wanders and is made to wander, beloved; robbed by its faults, (the world) weeps. If the Hukam of the Banker (God) is recognised, beloved, the True One is met, and glory comes. It is said to be hard to utter, beloved; how is the True Name to be heard? Those who have praised him, beloved: I am a sacrifice to them. May I gain the Name and be content, beloved; may I be united in union with the Gracious One. If the body becomes the paper, beloved, and the mind is made the inkpot, and the tongue the pen of Truth, beloved, then reflect on the Lord's virtues and write them down. Blessed, O Nanak, is the scribe, beloved, who enshrines the Truth in his heart and writes it. ॥8॥
636.2: Raag Sorath, a Dutuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). You are the Giver of virtues, the Pure One, O dear one; (our) mind does not become pure. We are offenders, without virtue, O dear one; that virtue (comes) from you alone. O my Beloved, you are the Creator: having made (me), watch over (me). I am a sinner, a hypocrite, O dear one: (grant that) the Name stand foremost in my mind and body. The poison of Maya has bewitched the mind, O brother; by cleverness (one) loses honour. The Master dwells in the mind through Truth, O brother, if the Guru's wisdom sinks in. Call (him) beautiful, beautiful, O brother: beautiful, a deep crimson. If the mind longs for the Lord, O brother, then at the door and in the home (of the heart) is the True One, who never errs. In the underworlds and in the sky are you, O dear one; in every heart are you, (giving) the knowledge of virtues. On meeting the Guru, peace is found, O brother, and pride has left the mind. Rub and scour the body with water, O brother, and still the body grows unclean. Bathe in wisdom, the supreme essence, O brother, and mind and body become pure. If one worships goddesses and gods, O brother, what am I to ask of them? What can they give? The stone (idol) is washed with water, O brother, yet such (stones) sink in water. Without the Guru the Unseen is not seen, O brother; the world drowns, having lost its honour. Glories are in my Master's hands, O brother; he gives them to whom he pleases. The bride who speaks sweetly, O brother, and in love of her Husband speaks the Truth, pierced by the pain of separation, dwells in the True One, O brother, and stays deeply absorbed in the Lord's Name. Each one calls (God) his own, O brother; (but) through the Guru (one) comes to understand the All-wise One. Those who are pierced (by love) are saved, O brother; the Shabad is (their) true seal. Gather a great heap of firewood, O brother, and put in it a spark of fire, (and it all burns away); (so) if the Naam dwells in the heart even for an instant, O brother, then, O Nanak, union (with God) comes with ease. ॥10॥
637.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, a Tituki, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Dear Lord, you ever protect your devotees; you have been protecting them from the very beginning. Dear Lord, you saved your servant Prahlad, and destroyed Harnakhash. The Gurmukhs have faith (in you), dear Lord; the manmukhs are led astray by doubt. Dear Lord, this (keeping your devotees' honour) is your greatness. Keep the honour of your devotees, O Master; the devotees are in your refuge. Jam cannot so much as eye the devotees; death does not go near them. The Name of Ram alone dwells in their minds; through the Name itself they have found liberation. All the riddhis and siddhis cling to the feet of the devotees, who (abide) through the Guru in Sahaj and in love. The manmukhs do not come to have faith; within them is greed and self-interest. Through the Guru, the Shabad has not pierced their hearts, and they have no love for the Lord's Name. The veneer of falsehood and deceit will come off; the manmukhs' speech is insipid. You yourself are at work within your devotees, dear God; it is the devotees who have known you. The whole world is in attachment to your Maya; you alone are the Being, the Creator. (Those who) have killed Haumai, and whose desire has merged into the mind itself, have recognised (you) through the Guru's Shabad. O God, you do the tasks of those who love the Lord's Name, and they are free of care. By the Guru's grace he ever dwells in their minds, the One who sets all tasks right. Whoever vies with those who have the Lord God as their protector is ruined. Without serving the True Guru no one has found (him); the manmukhs have died babbling and wailing. They come and go and find no resting place; in pain they are absorbed in pain. Whoever becomes Gurmukh drinks the Amrit, and merges in Sahaj in the True One. Without serving the True Guru the round of births does not let (one) go, though one perform countless rites in plenty. (They) read the Vedas and expound disputes; without the Lord they have lost (their) honour. True is the True Guru, whose Bani is true; those who run to the Guru's refuge are set free. Those in whose minds the Lord dwells are true at (his) door; at the True door they are found truthful. Their glory has shone in every age; there is no one who can erase it. Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who have kept the Lord enshrined in their hearts. ॥8॥
Riddhis and siddhis: wealth and the miraculous powers of yoga.
638.1: Raag Sorath, a Dutuki, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (God) himself forgives those without virtue, O brother, setting them to the service of the True Guru. The service of the True Guru is sublime, O brother; (through it) the mind is fixed on the Name of Ram. The dear Lord himself forgives and unites (us with himself). We are without virtue, and sinners, O brother; the perfect True Guru has taken (us) in among (his own). So many sinners has he forgiven, O dear one, through reflection on the true Shabad; he has carried (them) across the terrifying world-ocean, O brother, putting (them) aboard the True Guru's boat. From burnt iron they have become gold, O brother, as the Guru, the paras, joined them in union (with God). Once they gave up self, the Name came to dwell in their minds, O brother, and their light was merged into the Light. I am a sacrifice, I am devoted, O brother; to the True Guru I am ever a sacrifice, who has given (me) the treasure of the Naam, O brother; through the Guru's teaching I am merged in Sahaj. Without the Guru Sahaj does not arise, O brother; go and ask those who have wisdom. Serve the True Guru always, O brother, ridding yourself of self from within. Through the Guru's teaching the fear (of God) arises, O brother; that fear is the deed to be done, true and sublime. (Through it) the precious gift of love is found, O brother, and the True Name (becomes one's) support. Those who serve their True Guru, O brother: I fall at their feet. (Thus) I make my life worthy, O brother, and win forgiveness for my family as well. The true (Name), the Bani and the true Shabad, O brother, come by the Guru's grace. O Nanak, the one in whose mind the Lord's Name dwells, O brother, meets no obstacle at all. ॥8॥
Burnt iron (manur): iron burnt to slag. Paras: the philosopher's stone, held to turn iron into gold at a touch.
639.1: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The dear Lord is known through the Shabad, O brother; by perfect fortune (the Guru) unites (one with him). The happy soul-brides are ever in peace, O brother; keeping love (for him), night and day they are dyed (in it). Dear Lord, you yourself dye (the soul) in your love. Sing, sing (his praises), you who are dyed in his love, O brothers, with your love fixed on the Lord. She who does the Guru's work, O brother, giving up self and fixing her mind (on it), has Sahaj forever, and no pain touches her again, O brother; the Lord himself comes to dwell in her mind. She who does not know her Husband's Hukam, O brother, is an ill-mannered, unworthy wife; she does her work out of the mind's stubbornness, O brother; without the Name she is false. They alone sing (his praises) on whose foreheads there is good fortune, O brother; through love of the True One (comes) detachment. Dyed (in his love), night and day they dwell on his virtues, O brother; free of fear, they hold their attention fixed through the Guru. He kills all and brings them to life, O brother: serve him day and night. Why should he be forgotten from the mind, O brother, whose gift is so great? The self-willed (soul-bride) is filthy and double-minded, O brother; she has no place in the Lord's court. If she becomes Gurmukh, she dwells on his virtues, O brother, and meeting the Beloved she merges in the True One. One who has not remembered the Lord in this birth, O brother: what face will he show on going (there)? Even as the calls (of warning) were sounding, he let himself be robbed, O brother, lured by Maya. Those who cherish the Name dwell in peace, O brother; their bodies are ever at peace and calm. Says Nanak, O brother, cherish the Name of the Infinite, the Treasure of virtues, the Profound. ॥8॥
639.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. He who himself created the whole world, O brother, is the Cause of creation, all-powerful; he who fashioned the soul and the body, O brother, giving (them) his own power: by whom can he be told, how can he be seen, O brother? The Creator is One, beyond telling. Let us praise the Guru, (who is) Govind, O brother, through whom the essence (of all) becomes known. O my mind, let us repeat (the Name of) the Lord God, who gives the gift of the Name to his servants, and destroys pain and suffering. He in whose house is everything, O brother, whose storehouses are full of the nine treasures: his worth cannot be put, O brother; he is lofty, unreachable and boundless. He sustains all beings and creatures, O brother, and takes care of them day after day. Let us meet the perfect True Guru, O brother, who through the Shabad unites (us with him). Let the feet of the True One be served, O brother; (then) doubt and fear are destroyed. Joining the gathering of Sants, let the mind be scoured, O brother; (then one) dwells in the Lord's Name. The darkness of ignorance is dispelled, O brother, and the lotus (of the heart) blossoms. Through the Guru's words peace wells up, O brother; all fruits are with the True Guru. Let us give up mine and yours, O brother, and become the dust of all. God (Brahm) is spread out in every heart, O brother; ever present, he sees and hears. On the day the Supreme Lord is forgotten, O brother, on that day one dies in grief. He is all-powerful, and does and causes all to be done, O brother; he is full of every power. The Name is the precious gift of love, O brother, the end of attachment to Maya. When it pleases him he unites (one with himself), O brother, and the Name dwells in the heart. Through the Guru the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, O brother, and light dawns in the heart. God's glory has become manifest, O brother; earth and sky are in bloom. (The one whom) the perfect Guru has made content, O brother, is attached in love (to God) day and night. With his tongue he ever dwells on Ram, O brother; (this is his) true relish and aim. Hearing (the praises) with his ears again and again he lives, O brother; he has found the unmoving place. One to whom faith does not come, O brother: may that wretched soul burn! My Master has many virtues, O brother; I am a sacrifice to him. He cherishes the worthless, O brother, and gives a place to the placeless. He provides sustenance with every breath, O brother, he whose Name is of a deep colour. The one who meets the True Guru, O brother, has perfect fortune. Without him one cannot live for a moment, O brother; he is full of every power. With no breath or morsel is he forgotten, O brother; I see him ever present. In the Saadh's company (he) has united (me with himself), O brother, the One who fills all. Those in whom love (for him) has not arisen, O brother, die in grief day after day. Attaching (me) to the hem of his robe, he has carried (me) across the terrifying ocean, O brother, the world of pain. In his grace he has looked on (me) with his glance, O brother; he has taken (my) side beyond measure. Mind and body have become cool, O brother; the Name is (my) food and support. Nanak (has come to) the refuge of him, O brother, who cuts away sins. ॥9॥
640.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The mother's womb is an ocean of pain, O dear one; there (God) had (the being) repeat his own Name. Once (he) brought (it) out, the poison (of Maya) spread, O dear one, and (he) made attachment to Maya grow. The one on whom (God) himself has shown his grace, O dear one, he has united with the perfect Guru. That one worships (God) with every breath, O dear one, with attention fixed on the Name of Ram. In (my) mind and body is your support, O Beloved; in (my) mind and body is your support. There is no doer but you, O Beloved; you are the One, the Inner-knower. Having wandered through millions of births, (the being) has come (here), O dear one, suffering pain in countless species. (Here) the True Master is forgotten, O dear one, and great punishment is received. Those whom the perfect True Guru meets, O dear one, are attached to the True Name. Following those who are in the true refuge, O dear one, one is set free. What (one) ate taking it for sweet, O dear one, has brought disease into the body. It turned bitter and settled in, O dear one; from it grief has sprung. Feeding (beings) on pleasures, (God) has led (them) astray, O dear one; (their) separation does not end. Those whom (God) has saved by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, had their union ordained from the very Source. In one steeped in greed for Maya, O Beloved, you never come into the mind at all. Those who forget you, O Supreme Lord, O Master, their bodies have turned to dust. They wail a great deal, O dear one, (but their) agony does not leave. Those whom (God) has set right by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, their capital is kept safe. Do not keep company with a Saakat, O dear one, as far as it lies in your power, meeting whom the Lord is forgotten, O dear one; such a one rises and departs with a blackened face. The manmukh finds no shelter, O dear one; in the Lord's court he receives punishment. Those whom (God) has set right by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, succeed in full. A thousand disciplines and clevernesses, O dear one: not one has gone along (with anyone). Those who turn their faces from Gobind, O dear one, bring a stain upon their family. (They) have not known the thing that is (theirs, within), O dear one; falsehood has not gone along (with anyone). Those whom (God) has united with the True Guru, O dear one, cherish the True Name. Truth, contentment, wisdom and meditation, O dear one, (come to the one) on whom (God) casts his glance of grace. Night and day he sings his praises and dwells on his virtues, O dear one, filled to the brim with Amrit. They have crossed the ocean of pain, O dear one; they have gone across the terrifying world-ocean. Whoever is pleasing to you, you unite with yourself, O Beloved; they alone are ever genuine. God is the all-powerful Being, the merciful Lord, O dear one; the devotees lean on his strength. (The devotees) have fallen into the refuge, O dear one, of him who is the Inner-knower, the wise. (He) has set right this world and the next for them, O dear one; on their foreheads is the true mark. May that God never be forgotten, O dear one; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥8॥
In the Rahao and in the lines that speak to God as you, O Beloved addresses God; in the other lines, as the Darpan reads them, O dear one addresses the listener.
641.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. One has read the holy texts and pondered the Vedas, and practised nivli and bhuangam; (yet) the company of the five has not left, and (such people) are bound all the more by a proud intellect. O dear one, (the Lord) cannot be met in these ways; I have done many (such) deeds. Defeated, I have fallen at the Master's door: (O Master,) give (me) an intellect that discerns. One has kept silence, lived as a karpati, and wandered naked in the forest; one has roamed the river banks, the tiraths and all the earth; (but) duality does not leave. Driven by the mind's desire, one has gone to live at a tirath, and had the saw put to the head; but the mind's filth does not go in this way, though one make a hundred thousand efforts. Gold, women, fine horses and elephants: one gives gifts of many kinds; one offers grain, clothes and land in plenty; (yet) one does not reach the Lord's door. One stays absorbed in worship, the worship of images, bowing, prostrating and the six rites; (but) saying I, I, one falls into bonds; (the Lord) is not met by this method. The yoga of the Siddhs, the eighty-four postures: one has done these too, over and over, till weary. Living to a great age, one is born again and again, (for one) has not grasped union with the Lord. Royal pleasures, the pomp of kings, issuing commands none can refuse, a beautiful bed, sandal and perfume: (these are) the gate of terrible hell. The Lord's praise in the Saadh Sangat is the deed above all deeds. Says Nanak, it has come to the one whose due was written from before. Your servant is intoxicated with this love. The destroyer of the pains of the poor has shown mercy; this mind is dyed in the Kirtan of the Lord, Har Har. ॥1॥

Nivli: a hatha yoga practice in which the belly muscles are rolled to cleanse the bowels; bhuangam: by the Darpan, the serpent-shaped kundalini channel along the spine, up which the yogis draw the breath. The five: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride.
Karpati: one who uses his hands as his only bowl. The saw (karvat): by the Darpan, Shiva's saw at Banaras, under which some had themselves cut, hoping to reach Shiva's heaven.

The six rites (khat karam): the six duties of a Brahmin: studying and teaching, performing and officiating at sacrifice, giving and receiving gifts. The eighty-four postures (asanas) are the sitting postures of hatha yoga; the Siddhs are yogis perfected in them.

595.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Death comes to all, and parting comes to all.
Go and ask the wise who it is that meets (the Lord) hereafter.
Those who forget my Master suffer a very great anguish.
So praise, again and again, that True One,
by whose glance of grace there is lasting peace.
Praise him as the Great One: he is, and he will be.
You alone are the giver of all; no gift comes from a human being.
Whatever pleases him comes to pass; what is gained by wailing like women in mourning?
So many on this earth built forts and castles and went away, beating their drums.
Those whom the sky could not hold, he leads by a rope through the nose.
O mind, if you knew (these pleasures) to be stakes of torture, why would you eat the sweet?
O Nanak, as many faults as there are, so many chains hang about the neck.
If there are virtues, (the chains) are cut; virtues are one's brothers, one's true kin.
Those who go on (to the hereafter without them) are not accepted; (the command there is:) beat them and drive them out, these who have no guide. ॥4॥
595.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Let the mind be the ploughman and good conduct the tilling, modesty the water and the body the field.
Let the Naam be the seed and contentment the suhaga (the plank that levels the sown field), and humble living the guard (of the crop).
Then, by (God's) grace, love will sprout: see how such homes (hearts) grow rich.
O brother, Maya goes with no one.
This Maya has enticed the world; only a rare one understands.
Make your ever-waning life the shop, and the True Name the goods (in it).
Make awareness and reflection the storehouse, and keep that (Name) in it.
Trade with those who deal (in the Name), and take the profit, the gladness of the mind.
Let hearing the scriptures be your commerce; take truthful living as your horses, and set out.
Tie up good deeds as your provisions for the road; O mind, do not think that it can wait till tomorrow.
When you reach the land of the Formless One, you will find his mansion in peace.
Fix your mind (on him) and serve; make faith in the Naam your work.
Make the holding back of evil your running (on his errands); then everyone will call you blessed.
O Nanak, (the Master) looks with grace, and a fourfold glow comes over (the soul). ॥4॥
596.1: Raag Sorath, Chautuke, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To mother and father the son is dear; to the father-in-law, the clever son-in-law;
to sons and daughters their father is beloved, and to a brother his brother is most dear.
When the Hukam came, he left house and home, and in a moment all of it became another's.
The manmukh had no Naam, no giving and no cleansing: in that body he only raised dust.
My mind is won over by the Naam, my companion.
At the Guru's feet I fall; I am a sacrifice to the Guru, who has given me true understanding.
(The manmukh's) mind is pierced with false love of the world; he picks quarrels with the Lord's servants.
Absorbed in Maya, day and night he watches its road; he does not take the Naam, and dies eating poison.
He is steeped in foul talk and loves it; his attention has not turned to the Shabad.
He is not dyed in (the Lord's) love, nor pierced by (the Naam's) relish: the manmukh has lost his honour.
In the gathering of the holy he has not tasted Sahaj; his tongue has not a grain of (the Naam's) relish.
He took mind, body and wealth to be his own, and had no news of (the Lord's) door.
Blind, he walks on with his eyes shut; O brother, he does not see the house and the door (of the Lord).
Bound at Jam's door, he finds no resting place; he reaps what he himself has done.
When (the Lord) looks with grace, then I see (him) with my eyes; he cannot be told or described.
With my ears I hear and hear (his praise), and through the Shabad I praise (him), and enshrine the Amrit in my heart.
The Fearless, the Formless, the One without enmity: his perfect Light pervades (all).
O Nanak, without the Guru doubt does not run away; through the True Name comes honour. ॥4॥
596.2: Raag Sorath, Dutuke, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With the earth for the floor below and the waters (of the sky) for the roof above, your seat is the upper room (chaubara) whose walls are the four quarters.
All the worlds bear one image: your mouth (your word) is the mint that strikes them.
O my Master, your wondrous plays!
You fill and pervade water, land and sky; you yourself are contained in all.
Wherever I look, there is your Light; what is your form like?
Being of one form, you move about hidden (in all); yet no one is like any other.
The egg-born, the womb-born, the earth-born and the sweat-born: all are creatures made by you.
One wonder of yours I have seen: you pervade them all.
Your virtues are many; I have not known even one; give something (of understanding) to me, a fool.
Nanak humbly prays: hear me, O my Master; lift out the stone that is sinking. ॥4॥
596.3: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
I am a sinner, fallen, a great hypocrite; you are pure, the Formless One.
Those in your refuge, O Master, taste the Amrit and are steeped in the supreme relish.
O Creator, you are the honour of me, who have no honour.
Honour and greatness are theirs who hold the wealth of the Naam and are absorbed in the True Shabad.
You are perfect, we are lacking and shallow; you are weighty, we are light.
(Your devotees') minds are steeped in you alone, night and day and at dawn; O mind, repeat the Lord with your tongue.
You are true; we, absorbed in you alone and pierced by the Shabad, become true as well.
Those steeped in the Naam night and day are pure; those who die to be born again are unripe.
No other is seen; whom else should I praise? None is his equal.
Nanak, the slave of (your) slaves, humbly prays: through the Guru's teaching I have known that One alone. ॥4॥
597.1: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He is unseen, infinite, unreachable, beyond the senses; neither death nor karma has hold on him.
He has no caste, he is unborn and self-existent; he has neither attachment nor doubt.
I am a sacrifice to the True One, the Truthful.
He has no form, no colour, no outline; the True Shabad is his sign.
He has no mother, father, son or kin; he has no lust and no wife.
Without lineage, stainless, infinite, beyond the beyond: all light is yours.
In every heart God (Brahm) lies hidden; in each heart is his light, in all.
Through the Guru's teaching the hard (adamantine) doors are opened, and one sinks, fearless, into deep absorption.
Having made the creatures, he set death over their heads; he holds the ways of all in his power.
Serving the True Guru, they obtain the treasure; living by the Shabad, they are set free.
In a pure vessel the True One is contained; rare are those whose conduct is pure.
You have united the essence (the soul) with the supreme essence; Nanak is in your refuge. ॥5॥
597.2: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
As the fish (dies) without water, so the Saakat (the one turned from God) dies of thirst.
So, O mind, one dies without the Lord, with every breath that goes in vain.
O mind, take up the praise of the Lord's Name.
Without the Guru, how can I find this relish? The Guru unites (us), and the Lord gives (it).
Join the company of the saints: through the Guru, that is the place of pilgrimage.
Bathing at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage is had when the Guru's sight is attained.
As a yogi without continence, whose austerity has no truth and no contentment, (is in vain),
so is the body without the Naam: Jam strikes it, for the fault is within.
(The Lord's) love is not had from the Saakats; the Lord is found through love of the True Guru.
Says Nanak: one who meets the Guru, the giver of joy and sorrow, is merged in (the Lord's) praise. ॥4॥
597.3: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O God, you are the Giver, perfect in wisdom in your giving; we are your beggars.
What should I ask for? Nothing stays steady; O Lord, give me the Naam, that I may love it.
Banwari, the Lord, pervades every heart.
Hidden, he is at work in water, land and sky; through the Guru's Shabad, see and behold him.
The Guru, the True Guru, showing grace, has shown (me) this world, the underworld and the sky.
That God (Brahm) is unborn; he is, and he will be: see Murari (the Lord) within your heart.
This poor world is (bound) to birth and death; in duality it has forgotten devotion.
If the True Guru is met, the Guru's teaching is obtained; the Saakats have lost the game.
O True Guru, those whose bonds you break, setting them apart, do not go into the womb again.
O Nanak, the jewel of spiritual wisdom has shone forth, and the Lord, the Formless One, has come to dwell in the mind. ॥4॥
598.1: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The treasure of water for which you came into the world, that Amrit is with the Guru.
Give up costume, garb and cleverness: in double-mindedness this fruit is not (found).
O mind, stay steady; do not go wandering anywhere.
Searching outside, you will suffer great pain; the Amrit is in your home, within the heart.
Leave faults behind and run after virtues; doing wrong, you will regret.
You do not know good from bad; over and over you sink in the mud.
Inside you lies the filth of greed, and much falsehood; why do you bathe outside?
Through the Guru, repeat the pure Naam always; only then is the inner state raised high.
Cast off greed, give up slander and falsehood; through the Guru's word you will obtain the true fruit.
As it pleases you, so keep me, O Lord; your servant Nanak praises (you) through the Shabad. ॥4॥
598.2: Raag Sorath, Panchpade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You cannot guard your own house as it is being robbed; why do you go prying into the houses of others?
You will guard your house and door if you taste the relish (of the Naam), as the servant does who, through the Guru, is devoted (to service).
O mind, understand: what counsel have you taken up?
Forgetting the Naam, you are lured by other relishes; then, unfortunate one, you will regret.
You rejoice at what comes and weep at what goes; this pain and pleasure cling to you always.
He himself makes (beings) taste pain and pleasure; the Gurmukh stays free of attachment.
What can be called above the Lord's relish? Whoever has drunk it is satisfied.
The one enticed by Maya who has lost this relish goes and takes up the Saakat's evil counsel.
The mind's life, lord of the breath, master of the body: that radiant Lord is contained in the body.
If you give (it), then I sing the Lord's relish; the mind is satisfied, attuned in love to the Lord.
In the Saadh Sangat the Lord's relish is found; when the Guru is met, the fear of Jam runs away.
O Nanak, repeating the Lord's Name through the Guru, one finds the Lord, by the destiny written on the forehead. ॥5॥
598.3: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Over the head of every being is a writ, from the very beginning; no one is without a writ.
He himself is beyond any writ; making creation, he watches over it, and that One makes (all) move by his Hukam.
O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, and there will be peace.
Night and day serve at the Guru's feet; that Lord (alone) is the giver and the one who enjoys.
See outside the One who is within; there is no other at all.
Through the Guru, look with an eye that sees the One: the Light is contained in every heart.
Hold back the wandering (mind) and keep it in its own home; this understanding comes when the Guru is met.
Seeing the Unseen, I remain in wonder; pain is forgotten and there is peace.
Drink the Amrit, and the supreme peace is found; one comes to dwell in one's own home within.
Sing of (the Lord,) the destroyer of the round of birth and death, and there is no birth again.
The Essence, the Stainless One, his Light in all: Sohang (he am I); there is no division (between him and the soul).
The Infinite, the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), the Supreme God: O Nanak, the Guru who has been met is that very One. ॥5॥
599.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When I please him, then alone do I sing (his praise);
then (alone) do I receive the fruit of singing.
The fruit of singing comes
when that One himself gives it.
O my mind, through the Guru's word I have found the treasure;
through it I remain merged in the True One.
When the Guru's teaching awoke within,
then the restless intellect was given up.
When the light of the Guru's teaching shone,
then all darkness was dispelled.
When the mind clung to the Guru's feet,
then Jam's path ran away.
When, in the fear (of God), the Fearless One was found,
then (I) came to the home of Sahaj.
Says Nanak: only some thoughtful one understands
that in this world (true) deeds are what is excellent;
the (true) deed becomes (the Lord's) praise
when that One himself is met. ॥4॥
599.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O Lord,) the servants who have come to relish the Shabad all perform your service;
the one who has shed self-conceit from within has become pure, by the Guru's grace.
Night and day they ever sing the praises of the True One; through the Guru's Shabad their lives are made beautiful.
O my Master, we are (your) children, in your refuge.
You alone are the True One, ever true; you yourself alone are Murari (the Lord).
Those who stayed awake (and alert against Maya) have found God; through the Shabad they have slain Haumai.
Within household life the Lord's servants remain ever detached, reflecting on the essence of (divine) wisdom.
Serving the True Guru, they have found lasting peace, and have kept the Lord enshrined in the heart.
This mind runs off in the ten directions; in the love of another it has gone astray.
The foolish manmukh does not remember the Lord's Name, and has wasted his life in vain.
Once he meets the True Guru, he obtains the Name and is rid of Haumai and attachment.
The Lord's servants are true; they practise Truth, reflecting through the Guru's Shabad.
The True God has himself united them (with himself); they keep the True One enshrined in the heart.
O Nanak, from the Name have come liberation and wisdom; this (Name) alone is our capital. ॥4॥
600.1: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The treasure of devotion has been given to the devotees: the Name, the wealth of the Lord, which is true (and lasting).
Inexhaustible is the wealth of the Naam; it never runs out, and no one can set its price.
Through the wealth of the Naam their faces have become radiant; they have found the Lord, that True One.
O my mind, the Lord is found through the Guru's Shabad.
