Without the Shabad the world wanders astray, and in the Lord's court it receives punishment.
Five thieves live in this body: lust, anger, greed, attachment and ego.
They plunder the Amrit (of the Name), but the manmukhs do not understand, and no one hears their cry.
Blind is the world, and blind its conduct; without the Guru all is pitch dark.
Clinging again and again to I and mine, they come to ruin; nothing goes along with them as they depart.
One who becomes Gurmukh meditates on the Naam, ever keeping the Lord's Name cherished (in the heart).
Through the true Bani he sings the Lord's praises, and by the glance of the Gracious One he is made joyful.
Those in whose hearts the True Guru's wisdom is a light for ever: their command (holds) over the heads of kings.
Every day, day and night, they perform devotion; the Lord's Name is their true profit.
O Nanak, through the Lord's Name comes deliverance; those steeped in the Shabad are close to the Lord. ॥4॥
600.2: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
If one becomes the servant of (the Lord's) servants, then one finds the Lord, having shed self-conceit from within.
The work of the devotees is the bliss of the Lord, singing the Lord's praises night and day.
Steeped in the Shabad, ever constant in one hue, they remain merged in the Lord.
O dear Lord, true (and lasting) is your glance of grace.
Show mercy to your servants, O beloved, and keep our honour.
Praising (you) through the Shabad, I live for ever; through the Guru's teaching fear has fled.
My God is true and exceedingly beautiful; serving the Guru, my mind has become attached (to him).
One in whom is the true Shabad, the true Bani of the True One: that servant stays awake night and day.
(God) is most profound, ever the Giver of peace; his limit has not been found.
One who has served the Perfect Guru has enshrined in the mind the Lord, who is free of all care;
(his) mind and body are pure, there is lasting peace within, and he has dispelled doubt from within.
The way to the Lord is ever a hard path; some rare one finds it, reflecting on the Guru('s word).
Dyed in the Lord's love, intoxicated with the Shabad, he gives up Haumai and the vices.
O Nanak, he is steeped, constant in one hue, in the Naam of the One who adorns (lives) through the Shabad. ॥4॥
601.1: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O dear Lord, may I praise you ever, O beloved, as long as there is breath within my body.
If you, O Master, are forgotten for a moment, an instant, I count it as fifty years.
O brother, we had always been foolish and ignorant; through the Guru's Shabad there is light (within).
O dear Lord, grant (me) understanding yourself.
O dear Lord, I am a sacrifice to you; ever and always I am a sacrifice to your Name.
Through the Shabad we died (to self), and through the Shabad, having made us die, (the Guru) brought us to life, O brother; through the Shabad alone we have found liberation.
Through the Shabad mind and body have become pure, and the Lord has come to dwell in the mind.
The Guru's Shabad is the Giver; the mind dyed in it stays merged in the Lord.
Blind and deaf are those who do not know the Shabad; for what have they come into the world?
They have not found the Lord's sweet essence; they have wasted their life in vain, and are born again and again.
Worms of filth stay absorbed in filth: (so) the foolish manmukhs (stay) in darkness.
(God) himself creates and watches over (all), and sets (them) on the path, O brother; without him there is no other.
What has been written from the beginning, no one can erase, O brother; whatever the Creator does, that comes to pass.
O Nanak, the Naam has come to dwell within the mind, O brother; there is none other, no second at all. ॥4॥
601.2: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukhs perform devotion and are pleasing to God, uttering the Naam night and day.
You yourself take care of the devotees and protect them, (O Lord,) those who are pleasing to your mind.
You are the One who gives virtues, recognised through the Shabad; uttering (your) virtues, they merge in you, the Lord of virtues.
O my mind, ever cherish the dear Lord (in remembrance).
At the last moment he becomes your friend and helper, and he stands by you for ever.
The band of the wicked ever practise falsehood; they do not reflect and understand:
who has ever gained (good) fruit from evil slander? Harnakhash was torn apart by (the Lord's) claws.
Prahlad, (the Lord's) servant, ever sang the Lord's praises, and the dear Lord saved him.
They count themselves very good; in the manmukh there is no wisdom at all.
Engrossed in slander of the holy, they will depart having wasted their life.
They never remember the Lord's Name, and in the end they have gone, repenting.
(The Lord) has made the devotees' life fruitful; he himself has joined them to the Guru's service.
Steeped in the Shabad, intoxicated in Sahaj, they sing the Lord's praises night and day.
Servant Nanak makes this prayer: I fall at their feet. ॥4॥
601.3: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
He alone is (the Guru's) Sikh, friend and kinsman, O brother, who lives within the Guru's will.
Whoever walks by his own will, O brother, is parted (from the Lord) and suffers blows.
Without the True Guru he never finds peace, O brother, and repents again and again.
The Lord's servants are at peace, O brother:
(the Lord) has cut away their sins and sorrows of birth after birth, and himself joined them in union with himself.
All this family is bondage for the soul, O brother; the world is led astray by doubt.
Without the Guru the bonds do not break; through the Guru (is found) the door of liberation.
They do (their) deeds but do not recognise the Guru's Shabad; they die and are born again and again.
In I and mine the world is caught up, O brother, yet no one is anyone's own.
The Gurmukhs reach (the Lord's) mansion, singing his praises; they come to dwell in their own home (within).
One who understands here (in this life) recognises his own self; the Lord God is his.
Ever merciful is the True Guru, O brother; (but) without good fortune what can be obtained?
He looks on all with one (equal) glance; as is one's love, so is the fruit one receives.
O Nanak, the Naam dwells within the mind (when) one sheds self-conceit from within. ॥4॥
602.1: Raag Sorath, Chautuke, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
True devotion comes through the True Guru, (and) the true Bani (dwells) in the heart.
One who serves the True Guru finds lasting peace, and his Haumai is dissolved in the Shabad.
Without the True Guru there is no devotion; the rest of the world, ignorant, wanders astray.
The manmukhs wander about, ever in pain; they drown and die without water.
O brother, remain ever in (the Guru's) refuge:
he casts his glance of grace, keeps (your) honour, and grants the glory of the Lord's Name.
One who, through the Perfect Guru, has recognised his own self, reflecting on the true Shabad,
in (his) heart the Life of the World has come to dwell for ever, as he gave up lust, anger and ego.
(The Lord) is ever present, pervading all places; the infinite Naam (dwells) in (his) heart.
In every age the Bani has been recognised through the Shabad; the Name is sweet and dear to (his) mind.
One who, serving the True Guru, has recognised the Naam has come into the world with a fruitful life.
Tasting the Lord's sweet essence, his mind is ever satisfied; he sings (God's) praises, and through those virtues he is fulfilled.
The lotus (of his heart) has blossomed, and he stays ever dyed in (the Lord's) love; he has made the Anhad (unstruck) Shabad resound.
Body and mind are pure through the pure Bani, and he has merged in the True One alone.
No one can know the state (brought by) the Lord's Name; through the Guru's teaching it comes to dwell in the heart.
One who becomes Gurmukh recognises the way, and his tongue is soaked in the Lord's sweet essence.
Chanting, austerity and self-discipline all come through the Guru, as one enshrines the Naam in the heart.
O Nanak, those who cherish the Naam are beautiful; at the True One's door they have gained honour. ॥4॥
602.2: Raag Sorath, Dutuke, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When the True Guru is met, (the mind) turns back (from Maya), O brother; one dies while yet alive, and then gains understanding.
He is the Guru, and he the Sikh, O brother, whose light merges in the Light.
O mind, attune yourself in love to the Lord, Har Har.
O mind, repeating (his Name), the Lord comes to seem sweet, O brother; the Gurmukh finds a place in the Lord's presence.
Without the Guru love does not well up, O brother; the manmukh (stays) in the love of another.
The rituals the manmukhs perform are a pounding of husks, O brother; nothing comes into their hands.
When one meets the Guru, the Naam dwells in the mind, O brother, (and one is held) in true love and affection.
He ever dwells on the Lord's praises, O brother, through the Guru's boundless love.
The one who has come (into the world) is approved, O brother, who sets his mind on serving the Guru.
O Nanak, the Lord's Name is obtained, O brother, and through the Guru's Shabad comes union (with him). ॥4॥
603.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The three worlds are caught in the three qualities (of Maya), O brother; through the Guru understanding is given.
Clinging to the Lord's Name one is set free, O brother; go and ask those who have (spiritual) wisdom.
O mind, leave the three qualities and fix your attention on the fourth (state).
The dear Lord dwells in your mind, O brother; ever sing the Lord's praises.
From the Naam all have come forth, O brother; when the Name is forgotten, one dies (spiritually).
The ignorant world is blind, O brother; those asleep have gone, robbed (of their capital).
Those who awoke through the Guru were saved, O brother; (the Guru) carried them across the world-ocean.
In the world the (true) profit is the Lord's Name, O brother; (they) have kept it enshrined in the heart.
In the Guru's refuge they were saved, O brother, attuning their love to the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, the Name is the boat, the Name the raft, O brother; holding on to it, the Lord's servants get across. ॥4॥
603.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the world the True Guru is the ocean of peace; nowhere else is there peace.
Through Haumai the world is gripped by pain and disease; dying and being born again, it weeps and wails.
O mortal, serve the True Guru and find peace.
If you serve the True Guru, you will find peace; otherwise you will depart having wasted your life.
Under Maya of the three qualities they perform many rituals, but have not come to taste the Lord's sweet essence.
They perform the Sandhya, offer the tarpan and recite the Gayatri; without understanding they have found only pain.
Very fortunate is the one who serves the True Guru, the one whom (the Lord) himself unites (with the Guru).
Drinking the Lord's sweet essence, his servants are ever satisfied, having shed self-conceit from within.
This world is blind, and all of it acts in blindness; without the Guru the way is not found.
O Nanak, if one meets the True Guru, then one sees (God) with one's own eyes, and finds the True One within one's own home. ॥4॥
603.3: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without serving the True Guru, (the soul) is struck by great pain, and wanders through the four ages.
We are humble (beggars); you are the Giver age after age: through the Shabad grant (us) understanding.
O dear Lord, show mercy, O beloved:
join me to the True Guru, the Giver, and grant (me) the Lord's Name as my support.
With desire subdued, duality has merged in Sahaj, and the infinite Naam has been found.
Tasting the Lord's sweet essence, the mind has become pure; (the Name) is what cuts away sins.
Die through the Shabad, and then live for ever; then there will be no (spiritual) death again.
The Amrit Naam is ever sweet to the mind, (but) only some rare one obtains it through the Shabad.
The Giver has kept the gift in his own hands; he bestows it on whoever pleases him.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Naam have found peace; they alone are known (and honoured) in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
604.1: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When one serves the True Guru, the strain of Sahaj wells up, and only then does one gain the high spiritual state and true understanding;
the true Name of the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, and one merges in the Naam, in the Naam alone.
Without the True Guru all the world has gone mad;
the blind manmukh does not know the Shabad, and wanders astray in false doubt.
Led astray by the delusion of Maya of the three qualities, he earns (only) the bonds of Haumai;
birth and death stand over his head, and he suffers pain in the womb, birth after birth.
The three qualities hold sway over the whole world; in Haumai it has lost its honour.
One who becomes Gurmukh recognises the fourth state, and in the Name of Ram finds peace.
The three qualities all belong to you, (O Lord); you yourself are the Creator, and whatever you do, that comes to be.
O Nanak, through the Name of Ram comes deliverance, and through the Shabad Haumai is lost. ॥4॥
604.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Beloved (Lord) himself, all by himself, pervades (all); and himself, all by himself, he stays untouched (by all).
The Beloved is himself the world, the trader; himself he is the true Shah, the banker.
The Beloved himself is the trade and the trader; himself he is the true capital.
O mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and his praise.
By the Guru's grace is the Beloved found, (who is) Amrit, beyond reach, beyond all depth.
The Beloved himself hears and watches over all; with the mouth he himself speaks, from (every) mouth.
The Beloved himself leads (beings) astray into the wilds, and himself shows (them) the way.
The Beloved himself, he alone, is everywhere; himself he is free of all care.
The Beloved himself, all by himself, creates; himself he sets each one to his worldly task.
The Beloved himself brings about the making (of all); when he himself kills, (the being) dies.
The Beloved himself is the ferry landing and the ferryman; himself he takes (beings) across.
The Beloved himself is the ocean and the ship; as the Guru, the boatman, he himself steers it.
The Beloved himself boards (the ship) and crosses over; the King stages his wonders and watches them.
The Beloved himself, all by himself, is merciful; O servant Nanak, in his grace he unites (beings with himself). ॥4॥
604.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
(The Lord) himself is (all life) born of the egg, of the womb, of sweat and of the earth; himself the regions of the earth, himself all the worlds.
The thread is he himself, and the many beads are he himself; by his power he strings the world (on it).
The Beloved himself is the one who holds the thread; when he draws the thread out, (all) collapses into a heap.
O my mind, for me there is no other but the Lord.
In the True Guru is the treasure of the Beloved's Name; in his mercy (the Guru) lets the Amrit drip into the mouth.
The Beloved himself is in water and on land, everywhere; whatever God himself does, that comes to be.
The Beloved brings sustenance to all; there is no other, no second.
The Beloved himself has the plays played; whatever he himself does, that comes to be.
The Beloved himself, all by himself, is pure; himself he is (the one of) spotless glory.
The Beloved himself sets (his own) worth; whatever he himself does, that comes to be.
The Beloved himself is unseen, and cannot be seen; he himself makes (himself) known.
The Beloved himself is deep and profound; there is no other as great as he.
In all hearts the Beloved himself enjoys (all); in woman and man, everywhere, it is he.
O Nanak, the Beloved pervades (all), hidden; through the Guru he is revealed. ॥4॥
605.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Beloved himself, he alone, is everywhere; himself he sets up and pulls down.
The Beloved himself beholds (it) and rejoices; having staged his wonders, God watches himself (in them).
The Beloved himself is in every forest and every blade of grass, everywhere; through the Guru he himself is seen.
O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har: with the relish of the Name one is fully sated.
The Amrit Name is the supreme relish, so sweet; through the Guru's Shabad, tasting it, one comes to know it.
The Beloved himself is the tirath, the crossing place, and the raft; God himself crosses over, taking himself across.
The Beloved himself casts the net; the whole world, the fish, is the Lord himself.
The Beloved is himself unerring, and never errs; no other, no second, is seen.
The Beloved himself is the yogi's horn (singi) and its call; himself he plays the strain, and the one played is himself.
The Beloved himself is the yogi, the all-pervading Being; himself he practises austerities.
The True Guru is he himself, and the disciple is he himself; God himself gives the teaching to himself.
The Beloved himself has (beings) repeat the Name; himself he repeats it.
The Beloved is himself the Amrit; himself he is the relish, and he relishes himself.
The Beloved himself praises himself; O servant Nanak, (the Beloved) is sated with the relish of the Lord. ॥4॥
605.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He himself is the pointer, himself the scales; God himself has weighed (all) with the weight.
He himself is the banker, himself the trader; himself he has had the trade carried on.
The Beloved himself fashioned the earth, and set (only) a tank in the other pan (to weigh it).
O my mind, meditate on the Lord, Har Har; (whoever has done so) has found peace.
A treasure is the Name of the beloved Lord, Har Har; the perfect Guru has made it taste sweet (to me).
The Beloved himself is the earth, himself the water; himself he does and has (all) done.
The Beloved himself is at work through his Hukam; he has kept the water bound by the earth.
The Beloved himself instils fear (of him), and having tied the lion to the goat, he leads it about.
The beloved Lord himself is the wood, and he has kept fire within the wood.
The Beloved himself, all by himself, is at work: for fear of him, fire cannot burn (the wood).
The Beloved himself puts to death and brings to life; all who draw breath draw it as he has them draw it.
The Beloved himself is the strength and the support; himself he has set (all) to work.
As he himself makes us walk, so do we walk, O dear friend, as is pleasing to my Lord God.
The Beloved himself is the player and the instrument; O servant Nanak, (all the instruments) sound as he plays them. ॥4॥
606.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Beloved himself creates the universe, and makes the sun and the moon to give (it) light.
The Beloved himself is the strength of the powerless; himself the honour of those without honour.
The Beloved himself, in his mercy, protects (all); himself he is skilful and all-knowing.
O my mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the seal that grants passage.
Joining the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), meditate on the Lord, Har Har, and there will be no more coming and going.
The Beloved himself deals out virtues; himself he gives (them his) approval.
The Beloved himself bestows grace; himself he is the true seal.
The Beloved himself is at work through his Hukam; himself he is the decree.
The Beloved himself is the storehouse of devotion; himself he gives the gift.
The Beloved himself has (beings) serve him; himself he has honour bestowed (on them).
The Beloved himself sits in deep absorption; himself he is the treasure of virtues.
The Beloved himself is great; himself he is the foremost, acknowledged by all.
The Beloved himself sets the worth (of all); himself he is the scales and the weight.
The Beloved himself is beyond weighing, and himself he weighs (all); servant Nanak is forever a sacrifice (to him). ॥4॥
606.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Beloved himself sets (beings) to his service; himself he gives the zeal for devotion.
The Beloved himself has (them) sing his praises; himself he absorbs (them) in the Shabad.
He himself is the pen, himself the writer; himself he writes the writ (of each one's lot).
O my mind, repeat the Name of Ram with zeal.
Night and day there is bliss for the fortunate one; through the perfect Guru, earn the Lord's profit.
The Beloved himself is the gopi and Kanh (Krishna); himself he grazes the cows in the forest.
The Beloved himself is the dark and handsome one; himself he plays the flute.
The Beloved himself has Kuvaliapir (the elephant) killed; taking the form of a child, he destroys (him).
The Beloved himself sets up the arena; himself he stages the plays and watches them.
The Beloved brings forth (his own) form as a child, and slays Chandur, Kans and Keshi.
The Beloved himself is the strength; he breaks the strength of the foolish and the witless.
The Beloved himself creates the whole world; he keeps (it) in his power, and its way is in his own hands.
The Beloved himself puts the rope around (every) neck; as God pulls, so (beings) go.
Whoever is proud will be destroyed, O dear friend; O Nanak, repeating (the Name), one merges in devotion. ॥4॥
607.1: Raag Sorath, Dutuke, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Parted (from God) for countless births, (beings) have suffered pain; the manmukh does his deeds in pride.
Merely on touching the Saadh (the Guru), (I) have found God; O Gobind, (I am in) your refuge.
A love for Gobind, most dear, has taken hold (of me),
since (I) came into the true company of the holy, and Murari, who gives peace, has met (me) in the heart.
You dwell hidden in the heart, day and night, (O Lord); but the ignorant do not understand your love.
In the one whom the True Guru, the Being (Purakh), has met, God is revealed; he sings (God's) praises, reflecting on (his) virtues.
Through the Guru light has dawned, peace has come, and the evil-minded intellect has been cast out.
Recognising Brahm (God) within the self, peace has been found: (this is the gift of) your Sat Sangat, O all-pervading Lord.
The person who has found the Guru has met the Purakh, (the Lord): (so it is with all) on whom your grace has fallen.
O Nanak, (such a one) has found the peace of Sahaj, beyond all measure; night and day he stays awake, (absorbed) in Banwari, the Lord. ॥4॥
607.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
When love for the Lord pierces the inner mind, one cannot live without the Lord;
as a fish dies without water, so does one die without the Name.
O my God, in your grace give (me) the water, O Lord, of your praise.
Within (my heart), day and night, I beg for the Name; through the Name alone is peace found.
As the chatrik (rain-bird) cries out without water, and without water its thirst does not go,
(so) through the Guru one finds the water of peace, and in Sahaj, through love, through a love sublime, turns green.
The manmukhs, hungry, waver in all ten directions; without the Name (each) suffers pain.
He is born and dies, and comes again into (many) births; in the Lord's court he is punished.
If you show grace, (O Lord,) then we sing the Lord's praises, and find the Lord's relish within.
O Nanak, (the one on whom) the Lord, merciful to the meek, has become kind, his thirst has been quenched through the Shabad. ॥4॥
607.3: Raag Sorath, a Panchpada, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
When one consumes what will not yield (the mind's stubbornness), then success comes, and from that success understanding is gained;
when the arrows of love strike within the body, then doubt is cut away.
O my Gobind, grant this glory to your servant:
through the Guru's teaching make the Name of Ram shine forth (in me), and keep (me) ever in your refuge.
This whole world is coming and going; O foolish, unknowing mind, remember (the Lord).
Dear Lord, show your grace and unite (me) with the Guru; then (I) can merge in the Lord's Name.
Only God, whose thing it is, knows (it); the one to whom he gives it receives it.
The thing is beyond compare, utterly inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses; the perfect Guru makes the Unseen (Lord) seen.
Whoever has tasted it alone knows it, like a mute's sweet (of which he cannot tell).
Hidden, the jewel does not stay hidden, though one may try to keep it hidden.
Everything is yours; you are the Knower of hearts; you alone are the God of all.
Only the one to whom you grant the gift receives it; O servant Nanak, there is no other (giver). ॥5॥
608.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Tituke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Of whom should I beg, whom should I worship, when every one is (only his) creation?
Each one who seems great, and greater still, will be mixed into the dust.
The Fearless, Formless One, the Destroyer of the round of births, gives all comforts and the nine treasures.
Dear Lord, it is your gifts that satisfy me.
What is a poor mortal, that I should praise him? Why should I be beholden to him?
Whoever has meditated on the Lord, everything is his; (the Lord) has taken away his hunger.
The Giver of peace has given (him) such wealth as never runs out.
Bliss has come, and through Sahaj all comforts have settled (within); the True Guru has brought (him) into union (with the Lord).
O mind, repeat the Naam, worship the Naam, and speak the Naam night and day.
Hearing the teaching of the holy Sants, all subjection to Jam is ended.
Those to whom my God has been gracious are attached to the Guru's Bani.
Who can set your worth, O God? You are merciful to all beings.
Everything that happens is your doing; what are we, (your) children, O Gopal?
Save Nanak, your servant, (O Lord,) as a father is kind to his son. ॥4॥
608.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Chautuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O brother, the Guru, Govind, is to be praised, held firm in mind, body and heart.
That the True Master dwell in the mind, O brother: this is the most excellent of deeds.
Any body in which the Naam does not spring up, O brother, such bodies have turned to ash.
I am a sacrifice to the Saadh Sangat, O brother, to those whose support is the One Creator, Ekankar.
That True One alone is to be worshipped, O brother, from whom everything comes to be;
the Perfect Guru has made (me) understand, O brother, that without him there is no other.
Those without the Naam have wasted away and died, O brother; there is no counting them.
Without the True One, purity is not attained, O brother; the True Master is beyond reach.
Coming and going does not end, O brother; pride in the world is false.
The Gurmukh saves millions, O brother, giving (them) a single grain of the Naam.
The Simritis and Shastras have been searched through, O brother; without the True Guru doubt does not leave.
(One) grows weary performing countless rites, O brother, and binds (oneself) with bonds again and again.
All four quarters have been searched, O brother; apart from the True Guru there is no place (of refuge).
The fortunate one who has found the Guru, O brother, meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The True One is ever pure, O brother; pure is the praise of the True One.
The one on whom (he) casts his glance of grace, O brother, receives (this praise).
Among millions, O brother, such a servant is found: a rare one, here and there.
O Nanak, (such a one) is imbued with the True Name, O brother; hearing (this praise), mind and body become pure. ॥4॥
609.1: Raag Sorath, Dutuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As long as this one holds to love (for some) and enmity (for others), so long is union (with God) far off;
while one weighs what is another's against what is one's own, so long the screen of Maya stands between.
O Madhav, give me such understanding
that I serve the Saadh (the Guru) and hold to the shelter of his feet, and (that shelter) never slip from my mind for a moment, not for an instant.
O foolish, heedless mind, O fickle consciousness, it has never entered your heart
that, forsaking the Lord of your life, you are absorbed in others and entangled with enemies.
Sorrow does not grip one who does not set up his own self: this understanding I have gained in the Saadh Sangat.
The babble of the Saakat (one cut off from God) I take to be like a passing gust of wind.
This mind is covered over with millions of sins; nothing can be said (of it).
Servant Nanak, humble, has come to your refuge, O God: strike off his whole account. ॥4॥
609.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sons, wife, the people of the household, the women: all are kin only through Maya.
When the end comes, none of them will be of help; they are all false friends.
O man, why do you coddle this body?
It will drift away like smoke, like a cloud; worship the One alone, the Lord, the loving friend.
The body was made with three ends fixed for it: water, the dogs, or ashes.
Taking yourself to be immortal, you sit at home and have forgotten the Cause of creation.
In many a way (God) has shaped the beads, strung on a flimsy thread.
The thread will snap, poor creature, and then afterwards you will be sorry.
The One who created you and, creating, adorned you: on him meditate, day and night.
God has shown mercy to servant Nanak; I have taken hold of the True Guru's shelter. ॥4॥
609.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By great fortune I have met the Perfect Guru, and light has dawned in my mind.
No other can equal (him); my trust is in my own Master.
I am a sacrifice to my True Guru.
There is peace hereafter, the peace of Sahaj here, and bliss in my home (within).
The Knower of hearts, the Creator: he alone is my Master.
Fearless I have become, having fallen at the Guru's feet; the Lord's Name is my one support.
Fruitful is the sight of God, whose form is beyond time; he is, and he will be.
Holding his servants close to his heart, he protects them, in his own love and affection.
Great is his greatness, wondrous his glory; (my) task has been fulfilled.
Nanak has met the Perfect Guru, and all (his) sorrows are destroyed. ॥4॥
610.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one at peace sees all at peace; in the eyes of the sick, all are sick.
The Master does and causes all to be done; the joining (of each one's lot) is in his own hand.
O my mind, the one who has shed his own doubt,
in that one's eyes no one has gone astray: he has recognised God (Brahm) in all.
One whose mind has been cooled in the company of the Sants knows the whole world to be cool.
One whose mind is gripped by the disease of Haumai (ego) is born and dies, wailing.
One whose eyes have received the salve of (divine) wisdom sees light everywhere.
Lost in the dark of ignorance, (one) perceives nothing and wanders round and round.
Hear my prayer, O my Master: Nanak begs for this joy,
that where the holy sing your Kirtan, there my mind may be attached. ॥4॥
610.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have made my body the Sants', my wealth the Sants', my mind the Sants';
by the Sants' grace I meditated on the Lord's Name, and then all was well.
Apart from the Sants there is no other giver, no second;
whoever falls into the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru) is made able to cross over.
Through service to the Lord's servant millions of sins are erased, and the Lord's Kirtan is sung with relish.
There is peace here and a radiant face hereafter; the company of the Lord's servant is found by great fortune.
The tongue is one, (while the Lord's servant) is full of countless virtues: how much of his praise can be told?
The Unreachable, beyond the senses, the ever Imperishable (Lord) is found in the refuge of the Sants.
Without virtue, lowly, without a protector, a sinner, I have sought the shelter of the Sants.
Nanak is drowning in the blind well of attachment to home: (O Sants,) carry him through to the end. ॥4॥
610.3: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Creator, the one in whose heart you have come to dwell, that one's hope you have fulfilled.
Your own servant never forgets you; the dust of your feet is dear to his mind.
Your story is beyond words; it cannot be told.
O Treasure of virtues, O Master who gives peace, your glory stands above all.
The mortal does just those deeds that you have written (as his lot).
On the servant you have bestowed (your) service; seeing your sight, he is content.
You alone pervade all, through and through: (this is seen by) the one whom you yourself have made to understand.
By the Guru's grace (his) ignorance is wiped out, and he becomes known in every place.
He alone is wise, he alone attuned in meditation, he alone a person of loving nature,
says Nanak, to whom (the Lord) has shown mercy; from that one's mind (he) is never forgotten. ॥4॥
610.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All creation is gripped by attachment: at times (people are) high, at times low.
By no effort does one become pure; no one reaches the end (of it).
O my mind, release comes in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru).
Without the Perfect Guru, birth and death do not cease; (one) comes again, time after time.
That which is called doubt and delusion: the whole world is entangled in these.
The perfect devotee of the all-pervading Master stays apart from all things.
I speak ill of nothing in any way; this is the Master's making.
The one on whom my God has shown mercy has joined the Saadh Sangat and taken the Name.
The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, the True Guru delivers everyone.
Says Nanak, without the Guru there is no crossing over; this is the complete truth, well pondered. ॥4॥
611.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Searching and searching, having searched, I have reflected: the Name of Ram is the supreme essence.
Worshipped for even an instant, it cuts away sins, and through the Guru carries (one) across.
Drink the Lord's sweet essence, O wise one;
hearing again and again the Amrit Bani of the Saadh (the Guru), the mind attains supreme contentment.
Liberation, nourishment (of the soul) and the right way of life are had when the True One is found, the Giver of all comforts.
To his own servant he gives the gift of devotion, the all-pervading Being, the Creator.
Let us hear of him with our ears, sing of him with our tongue, meditate on him alone in our heart,
the all-powerful Master, the Cause of creation, from whose door no one goes empty.
By great fortune I have received this jewel of a human birth; be merciful, O Merciful Lord,
that in the Saadh Sangat Nanak may sing (your) praises and ever remember (you), O Gopal. ॥4॥
611.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Bathing and remembering one's own God, mind and body have become free of disease.
In God's refuge millions of obstacles have gone, and auspicious times have come to light.
The Bani of God, the Shabad, has been sweetly uttered:
sing it, hear it, read it every day, O brother; the Perfect Guru has saved you.
The True Master, of measureless greatness, the Lover of devotion, the Merciful,
has always kept the honour of his Sants; from the beginning he has kept to his age-old way.
Partake each day of the food of the Lord's Amrit Name; put it in your mouth at every hour.
Old age, death and fever have all fled; sing the praises of Gobind every day.
My Master has heard the prayer, and every strength has come about.
O Nanak, the Guru's greatness has become manifest throughout all the ages. ॥4॥
611.3: Raag Sorath, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Father is One, we are children of the One; you are my brother through the Guru.
Listen, friend: my soul will be a sacrifice to you again and again; show me the sight of the Lord.
Listen, friend: to the dust (of your feet) I am a sacrifice;
O brother, this mind is yours.
I will massage your feet, rub them and wash them; this mind I will give to you.
Listen, friend: I have come to your refuge; give me the teaching by which I may meet God.
One should not be proud; one should fall into (his) refuge, and accept as good whatever he does.
Listen, friend: soul, body, the whole self should be offered (to him); thus is the sight of the dear Lord attained.
By the grace of the Sants (God's) favour has come, and the Lord's Name is sweet.
The Guru has shown mercy to servant Nanak, and (he) has seen everywhere the Immaculate One, who has no lineage. ॥4॥
612.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Master and Lord of millions of universes is the Giver of all beings.
He sustains (them) always, caring for them and keeping watch; the fool (that I am) has not recognised a single one of his favours.
I have not known how to worship the Lord;
I just keep saying Har Har, Guru Guru.
O dear Lord, my name has come to be Ramdas, the servant of Ram.
Merciful to the humble, kind, ocean of peace, he fills all hearts;
seeing and hearing, he is always with (us); I, a fool, took him to be far away.
The Lord is boundless; I describe him within limits: what do I know of what he is like?
I make my prayer to my True Guru: give teaching to me, a fool.
What is one fool like me? Millions of sinners have crossed over.
Those who have heard Guru Nanak and beheld him are not cast into the womb again. ॥4॥
612.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The things I was so anxious about have all been wiped away and gone.
There is rest in Sahaj and (the bliss of) the Sukhmana channel; the inverted lotus (of the heart) has blossomed.
See, a wonder has taken place:
the Master whom (I) heard to be beyond understanding, the Guru has placed in (my) heart.
The fiends (the vices) that tormented me so have become fearful themselves;
they plead: save us from (your) Master; we are in your refuge.
Where the treasure of Gobind has been opened, whoever was destined to receive it has taken it.
The Guru has given me a single jewel; my mind and body are cooled and at peace.
The Guru gave (me) one drop of Amrit, and so (I have become) unshakeable and immortal: (I) do not die.
The Guru entrusted the treasures of devotion to Nanak, and then took no account (of him) at all. ॥4॥
612.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whose minds are absorbed in (the Lord's) lotus feet are filled and wholly content;
those in whose hearts (the Lord's) priceless virtues have not come to dwell stay parched with craving.
By worshipping the Lord one becomes free of disease and full of joy;
but for the one who forgets my loving Lord, it is as though a hundred thousand torments have come upon him.
O God, the servants who have taken hold of your shelter live at peace in your refuge, God;
those who have forgotten the all-pervading Being, the Creator, are counted among the wretched.
Those who, accepting the Guru, have fixed their loving attention on God have tasted the relish of great bliss;
those who forget God and turn their faces from the Guru have fallen into a dreadful hell.
To whatever (the Lord) sets anyone, to that alone he is set, and his ways are just so.
O Nanak, (those who) have taken hold of the shelter of the Sants are absorbed, within their hearts, in (the Lord's) feet. ॥4॥
613.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Just as a king is caught up in the affairs of kingship, and the proud man in the pursuit of honour,
and the greedy man is lured by the objects of his greed, so the wise are absorbed in the Lord's love.
This alone is pleasing to the Lord's servant:
seeing (the Lord) near and serving the True Guru, he finds his fill only in the Lord's Kirtan.
The addict clings to his intoxicants, and the landowner loves his land;
the infant is absorbed in milk: even so do the Sants love God.
The scholar is immersed in learning, and the eyes find pleasure in seeing;
as the tongue is lured by taste, so the Lord's servants sing the Lord's virtues.
Whatever the hunger, the Master of all hearts is the one who fills it;
Nanak thirsted for the sight (of the Lord), and God, the Knower of hearts, has met (him). ॥4॥
613.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
We are soiled, and you make (us) clean; we are without virtue, and you are the Giver.
We are foolish, and you are clever and wise; you know every art.
O Madho, such are we, and such are you:
we are sinners, and you are the destroyer of sin; beautiful is your land, O Master.
You fashioned all, and having fashioned them you honoured them, giving soul, body and breath of life.
We are without merit, with no virtue at all; you give (us) your gift, O Merciful One.
You do (us) good, but we do not recognise the good; yet you are merciful for ever and ever.
You are the giver of peace, O all-pervading Being, Creator; you protect your children.
You are the treasure, the eternal Sultan; all beings and creatures beg (of you).
Says Nanak, this is our state: keep (us) under the shelter of the Sants. ॥4॥
613.3: Raag Sorath, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the mother's womb, giving (us) remembrance of yourself, you were our protector there;
(now,) in the fathomless waves of the ocean of fire, carry (us) across, O you who carry (all) across.
O Madho, you are the Master over my head;
here and in the world beyond, yours is my support.
(Man) counts the made thing as great as Mount Meru, and holds the Maker to be a blade of grass.
You are the Giver, and all (the world) begs (of you); O God, you give (your) gifts as it pleases you.
In one instant (you make) one thing, in the next instant another: wondrous are your plays.
You are beautiful, hidden (in all), deep and profound, high, beyond reach and without limit.
When you yourself brought (me) into the Saadh Sangat, it was then that I heard your Word.
Nanak is in bliss at the very sight of the glory of the all-pervading Being, who is free of all desire. ॥4॥
614.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Beloved, I am the dust of the Sants' feet; I am in the Sants' refuge.
The Sants are my mighty support; the Sants are my adornment.
A bond has formed between me and the Sants;
I have received what was written for me from the past.
This mind has become your lover.
With the Sants is my giving and taking, with the Sants my trade;
with the Sants I have earned the profit: storehouses filled with devotion to the Lord.
The Sants entrusted me with the capital (of the Name), and then the anxiety of the mind was lifted.
What can Dharam Raj do now, when the whole account has been torn up?
Great bliss has come, and I have found peace, by the grace of the Sants.
Says Nanak, the mind is won over by the Lord, and I am dyed in the love of the Wondrous One. ॥4॥
614.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O man, as much of the world's goods as you see, all of it you must leave behind and go.
Trade in the Lord's Name, and you will attain the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled.
O Beloved, you are the One who gives me peace;
the Perfect Guru has given (me) the teaching, and I am threaded on you alone.
Lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride: in these no peace is found.
O my mind, become the dust under the feet of all; then bliss, joy and peace are found.
He does not let (anyone's) labour go to waste, and knows the state within: serve him, O mind.
Worship the Gurdev, whose form is beyond time, and offer up this mind (to him) as an oblation.
Gobind, Damodar, the merciful Madhav, the Supreme Lord, the Formless One:
(his) Name is (my) everyday provision, the Name alone (my) household goods; the Name is the support of Nanak's life. ॥4॥
614.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Guru) has put breath into the body of the (spiritually) dead, and brought back and united the separated (with the Lord).
Beasts, ghosts and fools have become listeners, and have sung the Lord's Name with their mouths.
See the greatness of the Perfect Guru;
(He) has pulled down the camp of pain and sorrow, and bliss and joy have made their dwelling.
The fruits the mind longs for have come unlooked for, and (all) tasks are fulfilled.
(There is) peace here, and faces shine bright hereafter; the comings and goings are ended.
Those who are pleasing to the mind of their True Guru have become fearless, and the Naam dwells in their hearts.
Rising and sitting, (he) sings the Lord's virtues, and pain, suffering and doubt have fled;
says Nanak, all his works come to fruition whose mind is attached to the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
614.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Leaving the jewel (of the Name), (people) cling to a cowrie shell, from which nothing at all is gained.
O my mind, one should always meditate on the all-pervading Supreme Lord, the Supreme God.
Remember the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O mortal;
this frail body will perish, O ignorant one.
(Maya is) a mirage and the longings of a dream: there is no greatness in it at all.
Without worship of the Lord, (nothing) will be of use; (Maya) goes along with no one.
Saying I, I, (his) span of life passes away, and he has not done what is of use to the soul.
Running and running about, he is never satisfied, and he has not come to know the Lord's Name.
Drunk on relishes, vices and the pleasures of the senses, he commits countless sins and is cast into the rounds (of birth and death).
This is Nanak's prayer to God: cut away my faults. ॥4॥
615.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sing the praises of the all-pervading, imperishable (Lord): this burns away the poison of lust and anger.
The ocean of fire is terribly hard to cross; in the company of the Saadh, one is carried across.
The Perfect Guru has wiped away the darkness of doubt;
worship (him) with loving devotion: God is near.
One who has drunk the essence of the treasure, the Name of the Lord, Har Har, stays filled in mind and body.
The Supreme God is present everywhere: from where would he come, and to where would he go?
Repetition (of the Name), austerity and self-restraint (are his), and he knows the essence of wisdom, in whose mind Gopal dwells.
One who has found the jewel of the Naam through the Guru: his labour has come to fruition.
Strife and suffering are wiped away, and all sorrows; the noose of Jam is cut.
Says Nanak, God has shown his grace, and mind and body have blossomed. ॥4॥
615.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God, who does and causes all to be done, is the Giver; God, the Supreme Lord, is the Master.
The Merciful One has made all beings; that God is the Knower of hearts.
My Guru himself has become my helper:
peace, Sahaj, bliss, joy and delight (are mine), and a wondrous glory has come about.
Those who have come to the Guru's refuge have had their fears destroyed, and are honoured in the true court.
Singing (his) virtues and dwelling on the Lord's Name, they have come to their own place.
Everyone hails and praises (me); dear (to me) is the company of the Saadh.
Forever I am a sacrifice to my own God, who has fully upheld (my) honour.
All who have had the sight (of the Guru) have been saved, hearing the discourse (of God), the wisdom and the Naam.
Nanak's own God has become merciful (to him), and he has come home in bliss. ॥4॥
615.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In God's refuge all fears have left; sorrows have perished, and peace has been found.
The Supreme Lord, the Master, has become merciful, and (I have) meditated on the Perfect True Guru.
O dear God, it is you who are my Master and Giver;
show grace, God, merciful to the meek, that, dyed in (your) love, I may sing (your) virtues.
The True Guru has made the treasure of the Naam firm (within me), and all anxiety is destroyed.
In his grace (God) has made (me) his own, and the Imperishable has come to dwell in the mind.
No obstacle touches the one whom his own True Guru has protected;
(the Lord's) lotus feet dwell within his heart, and he tastes the Lord's ambrosial essence.
Serve your own God as his servant, (the One) who has fulfilled the wish of your mind.
Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him who has kept (his) honour in full. ॥4॥
616.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Engrossed in the darkness of attachment to Maya, (man) does not know the Giver,
the One who fashioned soul and body and made (him); he counts the strength (he was given) as his own.
O foolish mind, God the Master is watching;
whatever you do, he knows it all: nothing at all stays hidden.
Drunk on the tongue's relishes and the wine of greed, (in him) countless vices have sprung up;
wandering through many births, he has suffered pain, (bearing) the loads of the bonds of Haumai.
Closing the doors, behind many screens, he sins with another's wife;
when Chitr and Gupt call for the account, who then will draw a veil over you?
O merciful to the meek, perfect Destroyer of pain, without you there is no shelter at all.
Pull (me) out of the ocean of the world; O God, Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
616.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord has become (my) helper; (his) story and Kirtan give peace.
Repeating the Word of the Perfect Guru, rejoice for ever, O mortal.
O brother, remember the True Lord;
in the Saadh Sangat lasting peace is found, and the Lord is never forgotten.
Your Name, O Supreme God, is Amrit; whoever remembers it comes to life.
The one who receives it by (your) grace becomes pure.
The mind is attached to the Guru's feet, destroyers of obstacles and dispellers of all sorrows;
singing the virtues of the unshakeable, imperishable (Lord), it stays awake night and day in the Lord's love.
The very fruits the mind longed for have been obtained; the story of the Lord brings peace.
In the beginning, the end and the middle, that God has become Nanak's friend. ॥4॥
616.3: Raag Sorath, a Panchpada, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(By which) attachment may perish, and (the sense of) mine and yours, and my clinging to what is my own may perish:
O Sants, tell me such a remedy,
by which I may rid myself of Haumai and pride.
(By which) I may accept the Supreme Lord (as dwelling) in all beings, and become the dust of (the feet of) all.
(By which) dear God may be seen with me, and the wall of doubt may fall away.
The medicine is the Naam, the pure water, the Amrit: it is found at the Guru's door.
Says Nanak, one on whose forehead it is written has (his) ills dispelled on meeting the Guru. ॥5॥
617.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 2, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
As fire lies hidden in all plant life, and ghee in all milk,
so (God's) Light is contained in high and low alike: Madho, the Lord, is in every heart, in all beings.
O Sants, (God) is contained in every heart;
he fully pervades all; the all-pervading Lord is in the water and on the land.
Nanak sings the glory of the Treasure of virtues; the True Guru has dispelled (his) doubt.
(God) dwells in all, yet is ever untouched; he is contained in all. ॥2॥
617.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He by whose remembrance bliss comes, and the fears and pains of birth and death perish,
(through whom) you gain the four great gifts and the nine treasures, and the hunger of craving does not come again;
he, taking whose Name you are at peace:
O soul, meditate on that Master with every breath, with mind, body and mouth.
(So) you will find peace, you will grow cool in mind, and the fire (of craving) will not smoulder within you.
The Guru has shown Nanak God in the water, on the land, in the three worlds and in the trees. ॥2॥
617.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lust, anger, greed, falsehood and slander: free (me) from these yourself, O God.
Cast them out from within this (mind), and call (me) near to you.
Make (me) know your own way yourself,
and let (me) sing songs of joy with the Lord's servants.
Put this way into (my) mind, that (you) may never be forgotten from (my) heart.
O servant Nanak, by great fortune (you) have met the Perfect Guru; (now) run nowhere else. ॥2॥
617.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The God by whose remembrance everything is obtained, and no labour goes in vain,
who is contained in all: forsaking him, where else are you absorbed?
O Sants, remember the Lord, Har Har, Gopal.
Joining the Saadh Sangat, meditate on the Naam, and (your) labour bears full fruit.
He looks after (all) and cares for them, sustains them always, and hugs (them) to himself with love.
Says Nanak, O God, forgetting you, how can (anyone) attain the Life of the world? ॥2॥
617.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Imperishable is the Giver of all beings; remembering him, all filth is washed away.
That Treasure of virtues is the devotees' provision for every hour; (yet) only a rare one attains him.
O my mind, repeat (the Name of) that very God, the great Gopal,
in whose refuge peace is found, and sorrow does not come again.
By great fortune the Saadh Sangat is obtained; on meeting (the holy), evil-mindedness is lost.
Servant Nanak longs for the dust (of the feet) of those who keep the Lord's Name strung in their hearts. ॥2॥
618.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(He) removes the sorrows of birth after birth and gives support to the withered mind;
on receiving the sight of him one is enraptured, and dwells on the Lord's Name.
My physician is the Guru, one with Govind.
He puts the medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, into the mouth, and cuts the noose of Jam.
O all-powerful, all-pervading Being, perfect Creator, you yourself are the Doer.
The Lord himself has saved his own servant; the Naam is Nanak's support. ॥2॥
618.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The state of (my) inner self you alone know; with you alone rests (my) judgement.
Forgive (me), my Master, my God: I go about committing hundreds of thousands of faults.
Revered God, you are my Master, ever near.
O Lord, (keep) me in the refuge of your feet; (I am your) servant.
O Master, you are countless and endless, lofty, full of virtues and profound.
Cutting the noose, (God) has made (him) his own humble servant: then, O Nanak, what need is there to beg of anyone? ॥2॥
618.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru, one with Govind, has become kind, and all the heart's desires have been fulfilled.
Clinging to the Lord's feet and singing the praises of Govind, (we) have become steady.
Good and auspicious is that moment
(when,) repeating the Naam, (one finds) peace, Sahaj and bliss, and the unstruck trumpets ring out.
(I) have met my own beloved Master, and home and mansion have become a source of peace.
Servant Nanak has found the treasure of the Lord's Name, and every wish (of his) is fulfilled. ॥2॥
618.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's feet have come to dwell within (my) heart, and God has brought forth auspicious marks (in my life).
The perfect Supreme God has become kind, and (I) have recognised within the mind the treasures of the Naam.
My Guru is (my) protector and friend.
He gives glory twofold and fourfold, and honour day after day.
God has saved all the beings and creatures who behold the sight (of the Guru).
Wondrous is the Perfect Guru's greatness; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
618.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I gather the pure wealth of the Naam, the lasting store of the unreachable, infinite (Lord).
O Sikhs and family, rejoice and enjoy delight, bliss and peace; partake (of this wealth) and live.
The Lord's lotus feet are (my) support.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), (I) have found the ship of Truth; boarding it, I cross the poisonous world (ocean).
The perfect, Imperishable (Lord) has become kind, and has himself taken care (of me).
Beholding (this) again and again, Nanak has blossomed; O Nanak, (God's kindness) is beyond reckoning. ॥2॥
618.6: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru has put forth his power, and (in me) compassion for every being has sprung up.
Uniting (me with God), he himself has given (me) honour, and all is well and at ease.
The Perfect True Guru is with me;
repeating (the Name of) the Supreme Lord, (I) am ever in rapture.
Within and without, in every place and space, wherever I look, I see him alone.
Nanak has found the Guru by great fortune; there is no other as great as he. ॥2॥
619.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Peace, joy, wellbeing and the strain of Sahaj (have come): (I) have beheld God's feet.
The Protector has protected the child; the True Guru has brought down the fever.
(We) have been saved in the refuge of the True Guru,
whose service never goes in vain.
There is peace at home and peace outside as well: our own God has become merciful.
O Nanak, no obstacle touches (us now); my God has become kind. ॥2॥
619.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru), zeal has arisen in the mind, and one sings the praise of the jewel of the Naam.
Remembering the Infinite, anxiety is wiped away, and the (world-)ocean has been crossed, O brother.
Enshrine the Lord's feet in (your) heart:
(whoever has done so) has found peace; the strain of Sahaj has welled up (within), and the whole heap of ills is wiped away.
Which of your virtues can I speak of and describe, (O God)? Your worth cannot be told.
O Nanak, the devotees have become imperishable, for their own God has become (their) helper. ॥2॥
619.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Troubles have gone and all ills have perished: our own God has shown grace.
Worship the Master at all hours: (thus) our labour has borne fruit.
Dear Lord, you are (my) peace, (my) wealth and (my) capital.
Save me: this, O brother, is my prayer before God.
Whatever I ask for, that very thing I receive; I trust in my own Master.
Says Nanak, (I) have met the Perfect Guru, and all anxiety has been wiped away. ॥2॥
619.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering again and again (my) own Guru, the True Guru, (I) have wiped out all sorrow.
Through the Guru's word, fever and ills have gone, and (I) have obtained the fruit the mind longed for.
(he is the form of) the Cause of creation, the all-powerful Master, the perfect, all-pervading Being, the Creator.
Sing (God's) praises in bliss, delight and joy: the Guru has become merciful, O Nanak.
Cries of victory ring out through the world: the Supreme Lord has become (our) protector. ॥2॥
619.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has not reckoned any account of ours; he keeps in view his age-old way.
Giving (his) hand, he has saved (us) and made (us) his own; (his servant) enjoys bliss for ever and ever.
Ever merciful is the True Master;
my Perfect True Guru has raised a dam (against sorrow), and all is well.
He who placed life within and fashioned the body, and gave clothing and food,
has himself kept his servant's honour; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
620.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord God himself has taken away the sin, and saved the whole world.
The Supreme Lord God has shown grace, and kept to his age-old way.
Ram, the King, has given (his) protection;
sing (his) praises in peace, Sahaj and bliss: mind, body and frame are at ease.
My True Guru is the Saviour of the fallen; my trust is in him.
Hearing Nanak's prayer, the True Master has forgiven all. ॥2॥
620.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, has shown his grace, and destroyed all ills.
In the refuge of the Perfect Guru (we) are saved; (he) has set right all (our) affairs.
The Lord's servant has remembered (him), with the Naam as (his) support,
(and) the Perfect True Guru, in his grace, has brought down the fever.
We rejoice for ever, my dear ones: the Guru has saved Hargobind.
O Nanak, great is the Creator's greatness; the true Shabad has been uttered, and it is the truth. ॥2॥
620.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My Master has become kind in that true court of his;
the True Guru has taken away the fever, O brother, and coolness has spread over the world.
(God) himself has protected his own beings and creatures; Jam has shut up his shop.
Keep the Lord's feet enshrined in the heart.
God should be remembered for ever and ever, O brother: he cuts away sorrows and sins.
In the refuge of him who has created everyone, (one) is saved, O brother.
He is the Cause of creation, the all-powerful, O brother; true is the renown of the True One.
Says Nanak, God should be meditated on, O brother, (and so) mind and body become cool. ॥2॥
620.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Sants, (bless me) that I may meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
may God, the Ocean of peace, never be forgotten, and may I obtain the fruit (my) mind longs for.
The Perfect True Guru, showing his grace, has taken away the fever.
The Supreme Lord God has become merciful, and the sorrow of the whole family is gone.
The Lord's Name, holding all treasures, the very form of joy and delight, is (our) support.
O Nanak, the Supreme God has kept (our) honour, and the whole world is saved. ॥2॥
620.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My True Guru has become (our) protector.
Showing grace, God has given (his) hand and saved (him); Hargobind is (now) whole and well.
The fever has gone: God himself has removed it, and kept the honour of his servant.
From the Saadh Sangat (I) have obtained every fruit; I offer myself as a sacrifice to the True Guru.
God has adorned both this world and the next, and has not weighed our merits and faults.
Says Nanak, O Guru, your word is unshakeable; you have placed (your) fruitful hand on (my) forehead. ॥2॥
621.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All beings and creatures are of his making; he alone is the helper of the Sants.
He himself keeps (the honour) of his servant, and (the servant's) glory has become complete.
The perfect Supreme Lord is with me.
The Perfect Guru has kept (my honour) wholly, and all have become kind (to me).
Nanak meditates night and day on the Naam (of him who is) the Giver of soul and breath of life.
He keeps his servant held close to his breast, as a father and mother (hold) a child. ॥2॥
621.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 3, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Meeting the village headmen, I was not rid of (my) anxiety;
from the chiefs I got no reassurance;
(I laid my) dispute before the nobles (too);
(but only) on meeting Ram, the King, was it settled.
Now I go nowhere searching,
for I have met Gobind, the Guru, the Lord of the earth.
When I came to God's court,
then all (my) outcry was stilled.
I have found what was mine to find;
then where is there to come, and where to go?
There, matters are settled by true justice;
there, master and servant are equal.
The Knower of hearts knows (all);
he himself understands without a word being spoken.
He is the King of every place;
there the unstruck Shabad resounds.
What cleverness (can work) before him?
O Nanak, shed self-conceit and meet him. ॥4॥
621.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Enshrine the Naam in (your) heart;
meditate on the Guru while sitting at home.
The Perfect Guru has declared the Truth;
(through it) that true peace has been found.
(Our) own Guru has become merciful;
having bathed, (we) have come home with bliss, peace, well-being and joy.
The Guru's greatness is true and lasting;
its worth cannot be told.
(The Guru is) the Emperor above the heads of kings.
On meeting the Guru, the mind fills with eager joy.
All sins have been shed,
by joining with the Saadh Sangat.
The Lord's Name is a treasure of virtues;
repeating it, (all) tasks have been fulfilled.
The Guru has opened up the door of liberation;
all creation hails him.
O Nanak, God is with me;
the fears of birth and death have left (me). ॥4॥
621.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru has shown grace,
and God has fulfilled our longing.
and have found bliss, joy and peace.
O Sants, through the Name of Ram one is carried across.
Rising and sitting, let us meditate on the Lord, Har Har, and do good deeds night and day.
The Sant's path is the ladder of righteousness; only some fortunate one finds it.
The sins of millions of births are gone for one who fixes his mind on the Lord's feet.
Ever praise your own God, who has kept his full power (at work in all);
all beings and creatures have been made pure, through the True Guru's teaching of the Truth.
Destroyer of obstacles, dispeller of all sorrows: such is the Naam the True Guru has made firm (within);
sins are cast off, all have become pure, and servant Nanak has come home in peace. ॥4॥
622.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(You are) the Master, fathomless in virtues;
(my) home and household, all are yours.
O Guru, O Gopal, you are (my) protector;
all beings have become kind (to me).
I abide in bliss, meditating on the Guru's feet;
in God's refuge, fear comes from no quarter.
O Murari, you (dwell) in the hearts of your servants;
God has raised (in them) a foundation that never shakes.
Your support is (my) strength and wealth;
you are my mighty Master.
All who have found the Saadh Sangat,
God himself has carried across.
In his grace (God) has given the sweet essence of the Naam,
and all is well and at peace.
God has become (my) helper;
all (the world) has risen and fallen at (my) feet.
Let us meditate on God with every breath;
O Nanak, let us sing the Lord's song of joy. ॥4॥
622.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Peace, Sahaj and bliss (have come);
God, dear to (my) mind, has met (me).
The Perfect Guru showed grace,
and then came my liberation.
(My) mind is absorbed in loving devotion to the Lord,
and (within) the unstruck vina plays always.
The shelter of the Lord's feet is strong;
all dependence on people has ended.
The Life of the world, the Giver, has been found,
and (I) have sung the Lord's virtues, relishing (his love) again and again.
God has cut the noose of Jam;
the mind's hope is fulfilled.
Wherever I look, there he is;
there is none but the Lord God.
In his grace God has protected (us);
all the sorrows of birth after birth are gone.
(I) have meditated on the Naam of the Fearless One,
and Nanak has found unshakeable peace. ॥4॥
622.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Creator has brought calm;
the fever has left the family.
The Perfect Guru has protected (us),
(when we) looked to the refuge of the True One.
The Supreme God himself has become the protector;
in a moment calm, Sahaj and peace sprang up, and the mind is at ease for ever.
(He) has given the medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
it has rooted out all the disease.
(He) showed his own grace,
and he has set every matter right.
God has kept to his own age-old way (of grace);
(he) has not weighed our merits and faults.
The Guru's Shabad has become manifest;
it has kept all (our) honour.
I speak what you have me speak;
You are the Master, fathomless in virtues.
Repeat the Naam, O Nanak: it is the true witness;
(God) has kept the honour of his own servant. ॥4॥
623.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Creator, the all-pervading Being, himself stood in the midst,
and not a hair was harmed.
The Guru brought the bathing to fruition;
repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, sins have been destroyed.
O Sants, the pool of Ramdas is beautiful;
whoever bathes (in it) carries his family across, and his own soul is set free.
The world sings (his) acclaim,
(and) he obtains the fruits his mind longs for.
(We) have bathed and come (back) safe and sound,
and have meditated on (our) own God.
Whoever bathes in the pool of the Sants
reaches the supreme state.
He neither dies nor comes and goes,
meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Only he understands this reflection on God
on whom God, the Lord, is merciful.
O brother, Nanak (has come) to God's refuge,
which has wiped out all worry and anxious reckoning. ॥4॥
623.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord has seen (his love for his servant) through in full;
nothing at all has been left wanting.
Attaching (his servants) to (his) feet, the Guru has carried (them) across;
(they) cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(God) is ever the protector of his own servant;
in his grace he has made (them) his own and kept them, and reared (them) as a mother and father would.
The fortunate have found the True Guru,
who has wiped out the road of Jam.
(Their) minds are set on the Lord's devotion and love;
repeating (the Name) they live, those fortunate ones.
(The Lord's servant) sings the Lord's Amrit Bani,
and bathes in the dust of the Saadhs' feet.
(God) himself has given his own Name;
God the Creator has saved (him).
The sight of the Lord is the support of (his) breath of life;
this is (his) complete and pure understanding.
Show grace, O Knower of hearts:
servant Nanak is in your refuge, O Master. ॥4॥
623.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru has joined (us) to (the Lord's) feet,
and (we) have found the Lord, ever with (us), our helper.
Wherever we go, there we are at ease;
in his grace, God has united (us with himself).
Sing the Lord's praises always, with love;
you will obtain every fruit the mind longs for, and (the Lord will be) a helper at the side of your soul.
Narayan is the support of (my) breath of life;
I am the dust of the Sants' feet.
(These Sants) have made the fallen pure;
in their grace, they have given (them) the Lord's praise.
The Supreme Lord cherishes (them),
ever beside the soul as its protector.
Let us sing the Lord's Kirtan day and night;
(then) one is not cast into births again.
The one to whom the all-pervading Being, the Creator, gives (this gift):
that one alone has known the Lord's sweet essence.
Jam's servant has not come near (him);
O Nanak, (he) has found peace in (God's) refuge. ॥4॥
624.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru has brought everything to fulfilment;
God pervades all, filling every place.
The bathing has taken place in peace and well-being;
I am a sacrifice to the Supreme Lord.
With the Guru's lotus feet enshrined in the heart,
not the least hindrance befalls; all (my) affairs have been set right.
Meeting the Saadh (the Guru), (people) have shed their evil-mindedness;
the fallen have all become pure.
Those who have bathed in the pool of Ramdas:
all the sins they committed have been washed off.
Let us sing Gobind's praises every day,
and, joining the Saadh Sangat, meditate (on him).
That one obtains the fruits the mind desires
who meditates on the Perfect Guru in the heart.
The great Gopal is bliss itself;
repeating again and again (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss, one lives.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam;
God has kept to his own age-old way. ॥4॥
624.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In all ten directions the clouds spread like a canopy, bank upon bank; the lightning flashes and frightens (me).
(My) bed is lonely, there is no sleep in (my) eyes: (my) Husband has gone away to a far land.
Now no message (from him) comes, O mother.
(Once,) when my Beloved travelled even one kos, four letters would reach (me).
How could this dear Beloved be forgotten, who has every virtue and gives every comfort?
Climbing up to the rooftop, I watch the road (for him), and my eyes have filled with tears.
The wall of ego, of I and I, has risen between (us); I hear that he is near, in (my own) land.
The screen (between us) is (as thin as) a butterfly's wing, yet, unseen, he seems far away.
The Master of all became merciful and wiped away all (my) pain.
Says Nanak, the Guru knocked down the wall of Haumai, and then (I) found Bithal, the Merciful.
All (my) anxiety is gone, O mother;
the Guru has brought (me) to the one I longed for:
the King, the treasure of every virtue. ॥11॥
624.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord, you are) the Restorer of what was lost, the Releaser of captives, the Formless One, the Healer of pain.
I know nothing of good deeds, nothing of Dharma; I am greedy, clinging to Maya.
(Yet) I have come to be called Govind's devotee: keep this honour, which is yours.
Dear Lord, you are the honour of those without honour;
my Govind makes the worthless precious; I am a sacrifice to your might.
Just as a child, out of fondness and its own nature, commits a hundred thousand faults,
and the father, teaching it, scolds it in many ways, and then holds it close again,
(so) God forgives past failings and sets (one) on the path for what lies ahead.
The Lord, the Knower of hearts, knows every state; to whom else, then, should one tell it?
Gobind is not won over by mere talk and telling; if it pleases the Lord, (one's) honour is kept.
I have looked at every other shelter; yours is the one shelter I keep.
God the Master, kind and merciful, himself hears the prayer,
brings (one) to meet the Perfect True Guru, and all the mind's anxiety ends.
The medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has been put into (my) mouth; servant Nanak dwells in peace. ॥4॥
625.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering God over and over, (we) have come into bliss; all pain and strife have fled.
Singing the praises of our God and meditating on him, all (our) affairs have been set in order.
(O God,) your Name is the life of all the world.
From the Perfect Guru (we) received the teaching; repeating (the Name), (we) have been carried across the terrifying world-ocean.
You alone are (your own) counsellor, O God, and you hear (all); you alone are able to do all things.
It is you who give and you who enjoy; of what account is this poor creature?
What virtues of yours could I speak of and describe? Your worth cannot be told.
Beholding his God again and again, (one) lives; wondrous is your greatness.
O God, my Master, showing your favour, you yourself have made (my) honour and understanding whole.
Nanak is a sacrifice for ever and ever; I long for the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
625.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever) bows to the Perfect Guru:
God has set right all (his) affairs.
The Lord has shown his grace;
God has fully upheld (his) honour.
(God) has become the helper of his servant;
the Creator has fulfilled every wish; nothing is left wanting.
The Creator, the all-pervading Being, has had the pool made;
Maya has followed along behind;
there is no shortage anywhere.
So it pleases my Perfect True Guru.
Remembering the Merciful One again and again,
all beings have become kind (to me).
All acclaim to the Lord of the world,
who has made the whole design complete.
You are my great Master;
this treasure is your own gift.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the One,
and has received the blessing that bears every fruit. ॥4॥
625.3: Raag Sorath, Ghar 3, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who have bathed in the pool of Ramdas:
all the sins they committed have been washed away;
this is the gift of the Perfect Guru.
God has bestowed all peace and well-being;
everything has been kept safe and sound, by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
In the Saadh Sangat the filth (of the mind) has been washed off;
the Supreme Lord has become (our) companion.
Nanak has meditated on the Naam,
and has found God, the Primal Being. ॥2॥
625.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The (house of the heart) in which the Supreme Lord has come to mind:
that house the Master has made to flourish.
When (one) found the Guru, the Ocean of peace,
The glory of the Lord's Name,
the singing of (his) praises at all hours:
(this gift I) have received from the Perfect Guru.
The story of God is beyond telling;
his servants speak the Bani that is Amrit.
having come to know (it) through the Perfect Guru. ॥2॥
626.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ahead, (in the world beyond,) the Guru has given peace;
behind, (in this world,) too, the Guru has brought peace and well-being.
(I) have found all treasures and comforts,
(for I) have meditated on my Guru in (my) heart.
(Such is) the greatness of my own True Guru:
(through him) one obtains the fruits the mind longs for;
O Sants, (this greatness) grows more and more, day by day.
All beings and creatures have become kind (to me); God has made (them) his own.
Gopal has been met, naturally, in Sahaj; O Nanak, (they) have found contentment in the True One. ॥2॥
626.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
a watch kept all around us.
The mind is fixed on the Name of Ram;
Dear God, it is you who give me peace;
cutting away the bonds (of Maya), the perfect, all-pervading Being, the Creator, makes the mind pure.
service done to him will not go in vain.
repeating (your Name), (their) hope has been fulfilled. ॥2॥
626.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to my Guru,
(I) have found the fruit the mind longed for,
(for I) have always meditated on my God.
O Sants, without him there is no other;
that God alone is the Cause of creation.
My own God has granted blessings,
and has brought all beings under (his) sway.
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam,
and so (he) has wiped out all (his) sorrows. ॥2॥
626.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The perfect Guru has taken away the fever;
God has brought about every blessing;
he himself has given them, out of his mercy.
The True Guru himself has taken away the pain;
all the Sikhs and Sants, meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have become full of joy.
Whatever (your Sants) ask for, they receive;
O God, you (yourself) give to your own Sants.
servant Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the True One. ॥2॥
626.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) have (me) do only what pleases you;
I have no cleverness at all.
We, (your) children, are in your refuge;
O Lord King, (you are) my mother and father;
in your mercy you have taken (me) into your care; I do what you have me do.
All beings and creatures are upheld by you;
O God, (their) string is in your hands.
whatever he has (us) do, that alone is done;
servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥2॥
627.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's Name has been threaded into the heart,
(and so) all our work has been done.
The mind of that one has become attached to God's feet
Joining the Saadh Sangat, (I) have meditated on the Lord;
at all hours (I) have worshipped the Lord, Har Har, and have found the fruit the mind longed for.
The shoot (of deeds) from lives long past has sprung up,
(and) the mind has become attached to the Name of Ram.
Staying absorbed, in mind and body, in the sight of the Lord,
servant Nanak sings the praises of the True One. ॥2॥
627.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever), meeting the Guru, has remembered God
O Sants, the Master's refuge is the one that stands for ever;
all beings and creatures are in his hands alone; that God is the Knower of hearts.
God has kept to his own age-old way (of grace).
servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to it). ॥2॥
627.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord fashioned (this child) and made (him) fair;
