the Guru has saved this little one.
the Supreme God is the giver of life.
you keep the honour of your servant, and set (his) affairs right yourself.
My God does good to others,
he who has set his full power (in all creation).
and has found the fruit the mind longed for. ॥2॥
627.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat (the Name of) the Lord for ever and ever;
God himself is the protector of children.
through the Lord's praise the dangers have gone.
My God has ever been merciful;
he has heard the prayer of his devotee, and has become kind to all beings.
God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful;
remembering the Lord, all pain has gone.
(He) has heard the plea of his servant;
O Nanak, all the world sleeps in peace. ॥2॥
627.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(and) meeting (him), (we) have come home safe and well.
(This is) the glory of the Naam;
O Sants, worship the Lord, Har, Har, Har;
worshipping the Lord, everything is obtained: (so) bring all (your) tasks to fulfilment.
Loving devotion to God has taken hold (of the mind);
only that one receives (this gift) whose fortune is great.
O servant Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam
has found the fruit that gives every comfort. ॥2॥
627.6: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme God has raised a dam (against misfortune),
(and) has broken up the camp of pain and disease.
God, the Lord, Har Har, has shown mercy.
O Sants, there is peace everywhere;
the Supreme Lord, the perfect Supreme God, pervades every place.
The Bani has come from God, the very source;
it has wiped away all anxiety.
The merciful Being has been kind;
Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the Lord, the True One. ॥2॥
628.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Here and hereafter (he is) the protector:
God, the True Guru, merciful to the meek.
in every heart (it is he who) speaks the word.
I offer myself as a sacrifice at the Guru's feet;
day and night, with every breath, I keep in mind (God), who pervades all places.
true is the gift of the True One.
Devotion to you and your praise
Nanak has found in your refuge, O God. ॥2॥
628.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When it pleased the perfect True Guru,
then (I) repeated the Name of Ram.
The Lord's feet ever give peace;
whatever (those who hold to them) wish for, that very fruit they receive; (their) hope does not go empty.
The one on whom the Lord of life, the Giver, shows mercy: that Sant alone sings (his) praises.
his mind is absorbed in loving devotion, and he is pleasing to the mind of the Supreme Lord.
With the Lord's praise uttered at all hours, the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures has worn off.
My Creator has united (me) with himself; the Sants, the holy ones, have become (my) companions.
He has taken (me) by the hand, given (me) all things, and himself joined (me) to himself.
Says Nanak, every undertaking has been fulfilled: (I) have found the perfect True Guru. ॥4॥
628.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(to be) the dust and ashes beneath the feet of all is (our) double-edged sword.
Before this no evildoer can stand;
the perfect Guru has taught this.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the shelter of the Sants;
whoever remembers it is set free, and millions upon millions are saved.
In the company of the Sants (I) have sung (his) praise,
(and) have found this perfect wealth of the Lord.
(and) everywhere the Supreme Lord has come into view. ॥2॥
628.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The perfect Guru has shown (his) full (grace),
(I) have found lasting bliss and peace;
(he) has made every place dwell in peace.
Devotion to the Lord gives (every) fruit;
the perfect Guru in his mercy has given it; only some rare one has known it.
Let us sing Gurbani, O brother;
it ever bears fruit and gives peace.
O Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam
has received what was written for him beforehand. ॥2॥
628.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Sants, repeating (the Name of) Ram, (I) have found peace;
(I) have come to dwell in the abode of the Sants in peace and Sahaj, and have wiped away all sorrows.
The Bani of the perfect Guru
is pleasing to the mind of the Supreme Lord.
(it is) the pure story of the One beyond words. ॥2॥
629.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
A hungry man feels no shame in eating;
just so does the Lord's servant sing the Lord's praises.
Why be slack about our own task,
the remembrance through which the face is bright in the Lord's court, and peace is found for ever and ever?
As the lustful man is lured by lust,
so the Lord's praise is dear to the Lord's servant.
As a mother clings to her child,
so the one who knows (God) practises the Naam.
(The one who) receives (this gift) from the perfect Guru,
O servant Nanak, (he alone) meditates on the Naam. ॥4॥
629.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(I) have come home in peace and well-being;
ash has fallen on the slanderer's face.
The Perfect Guru has robed (me) in honour,
O Sants, this is the greatness of the True One,
who has brought about a wondrous glory.
the servant utters the Bani and proclaims God.
O Nanak, God is the Giver of peace,
who has made a perfect arrangement. ॥2॥
629.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meditating on our own God in the heart,
(we) have come home safe and sound.
Contentment has come about in the world;
the Perfect Guru has taken hold of (us) and carried (us) across.
O Sants, my God is ever merciful.
He does not count up the account of his devotee; Gopal protects his children.
Whoever keeps the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart
has set all things in order.
The Perfect Guru, pleased, has given (the gift of the Name);
since then, O Nanak, there has been no sorrow. ॥2॥
629.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That same Lord has come to dwell in (my) mind and body;
This is the greatness of the Perfect Guru;
I am a sacrifice to your Name.
O my Beloved, the one whom you forgive sings your praise.
the Sants put their trust in you.
O God, Nanak has come to your refuge;
ash is on the slanderer's face. ॥2॥
629.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ahead, in the world to come, there is peace, my friend,
and behind, in this world, bliss: God has brought it about.
The Supreme God has made such an arrangement
(My) mind has come to trust the True Master;
(I) have known the Lord to be in all, through and through.
All beings are yours, O Merciful One;
Nanak meditates on the Naam every day. ॥2॥
630.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Death's messenger does not come near (me).
Holding (me) close to his bosom, God protects (me):
(this is) owing to the True Guru's teaching of the Truth.
The Perfect Guru has made all complete:
he has struck down and routed all the enemies, and given his servant good understanding.
God has made all the places flourish;
(we) have come back in peace and well-being.
Nanak has come to the refuge of God,
who has wiped away all diseases. ॥2॥
630.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The True Guru is the Giver of all comforts; let us fall into his refuge.
On receiving the sight of him bliss arises and sorrow has gone; let us sing of the Lord.
Drink the Lord's sweet essence, O brother;
repeat the Naam, worship the Naam alone, in the refuge of the Perfect Guru.
It comes to him alone for whom it is written from the start; he alone is perfect, O brother.
Dear God, this is Nanak's prayer: that I may stay with my mind attuned to the Naam. ॥2॥
630.3: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, who does and causes all to be done, the Knower of hearts, keeps (the honour) of his own servant;
(that servant) is hailed throughout the world, and tastes the sweet essence of the Guru's Shabad.
Dear God, O Lord of the world, I have your shelter.
You are all-powerful, the Giver of refuge; at all hours I meditate on you.
O God, the servant who worships you has no anxiety;
touching the True Guru's feet, his fear is wiped away, and he has sung the Lord's praises in his mind.
O True Guru, those you have comforted (have) peace, Sahaj and bliss in plenty;
victorious, they have come home with honour, and their hope is fulfilled.
The Guru is perfect, and perfect is his teaching; the works of God are perfect.
Clinging to the Guru's feet and repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Nanak has crossed the world-ocean. ॥4॥
630.4: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The destroyer of the pains of the poor has become merciful; he himself has arranged everything.
He has saved his own servant in an instant; the Perfect Guru has cut through (his) fetters.
O my mind, let us always meditate on the Guru, Govind;
all troubles are wiped from this body, and one obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
The God by whom all beings and creatures were made is lofty, beyond reach, without limit.
In the Saadh Sangat Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and (his) face is radiant in the Lord's court. ॥2॥
630.5: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
day and night I meditate on him always,
who has given his hand and saved (his servants);
they have tasted the Lord's Name, the supreme sweet essence.
(I am) a sacrifice to my own Guru:
the perfect God, the Giver, has become merciful, and (all) beings have become kind (to me).
Servant Nanak has come to the refuge of the One
who has kept (his) honour in full
631.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hear (my) prayer, O my Master: all beings and creatures are upheld by you.
Keep the honour of your own Name, O you who do and cause all to be done.
Dear God, my Beloved, do a Master's part by (us):
bad or good, we are yours.
The almighty Master has heard the plea; cutting away (their) bonds, he has made (them) fair.
Dressing his servants in robes of honour, he has joined them (to himself); O Nanak, they have become known throughout the world. ॥2॥
631.2: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has made all beings and creatures subject (to his servants), and all (his) servants (are honoured) at (his) court.
God has taken his own as his own, and carried them across the world-ocean.
He has set right all the affairs of the Sants,
our perfect Master, merciful to the meek, kind, the treasure of mercy.
Bidden come and sit, (they are) honoured everywhere, and lack nothing in any way.
He has given his servants the robe of honour of devotion; O Nanak, God's glory has become known. ॥2॥
631.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mind, give your love to Ram;
let your ears hear Gobind's praises, and your tongue sing (his) songs.
Join the Saadh Sangat and remember Madho; (so) the fallen become pure.
Death roams like a snake, its jaws spread wide, my friend.
Today or tomorrow it will swallow you too; grasp this and hold it in your mind.
Says Nanak: worship Ram; the moment is passing. ॥2॥
631.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
The mind's longing has stayed within the mind itself:
(he) neither worshipped the Lord nor served the holy, who are the true tiraths, and Death has seized (him) by the hair.
Wife, friends, sons, chariots, property, wealth, the whole earth entire:
know these and all else to be false; only the worship of Ram is real.
Wandering on and on through many ages you grew weary, and (now) you have gained the human body.
Says Nanak: this is your turn to meet (him); why do you not remember (him)? ॥2॥
631.5: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, what evil understanding have you taken up?
You are wrapped up in the relish of other men's wives and of slander, and have not practised devotion to Ram.
You have not known the path of liberation, and have run about to amass wealth.
In the end no one has kept (anyone) company; you have had yourself bound for nothing.
You have neither worshipped the Lord nor served the Guru, and no wisdom at all has welled up (in you).
The Stainless One is right within your own heart, and you search the wilderness (for him).
Wandering through many births you have grown weary, yet have not gained a steady understanding.
Having gained the station of the human body, worship the Lord: this is the counsel Nanak has given. ॥3॥
632.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, reflect upon the refuge of God;
Ganika was saved by remembering him: keep his praise enshrined in your heart.
By remembering him Dhru became immovable and reached the fearless state;
such a Master, the remover of sorrow: why have you forgotten him?
The moment he took the shelter of the treasure of mercy, Gaj, the elephant, was freed from the crocodile.
How far can I tell the glory of the Name? As he uttered Ram, his bond was broken.
The world knows Ajamal as a sinner; in the twinkling of an eye he was carried across.
Says Nanak: remember (God), the wish-fulfilling jewel, and you too will cross over. ॥3॥
632.2: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
What means should a mortal take up,
by which he may gain devotion to Ram and shake off the dread of Jam?
Tell me: what deeds, what sort of learning, and then what dharma should he practise?
Which Name is it, O Guru, by remembering which one may cross the world-ocean?
In Kalyug the Name of the treasure of mercy is the one (way); whoever repeats it attains liberation.
No other dharma equals it; so the Veda declares.
He whom (people) call the Lord of the world is beyond pleasure and pain, ever untouched;
O Nanak, he dwells within you yourself, through and through, like (a reflection) in a mirror. ॥3॥
632.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mother, how am I to recognise the Lord of the world?
My mind remains entangled in great attachment, in the darkness of ignorance.
I have wasted my whole life wandering in doubt upon doubt, and have not gained a steady understanding.
Night and day I have stayed attached to the pleasures of the senses, and (my) baseness has not left me.
I have never kept the Saadh Sangat, nor sung the praises of God.
In me, servant Nanak, there is no virtue at all; keep me safe in your refuge. ॥2॥
632.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mother, my mind is not in my power.
Night and day it runs after the pleasures of the senses; by what means am I to hold it back?
It hears the teachings of the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, yet does not let them dwell in the heart for a single moment;
absorbed in others' wealth and others' wives, it passes its life in vain.
In the intoxication of Maya it has gone mad; it has no inkling of wisdom at all.
The Stainless One dwells within the heart itself, (yet) it has not known his secret.
As soon as it came to the refuge of the Saadh, all (its) evil understanding was destroyed;
then, O Nanak, it remembered (God), the wish-fulfilling jewel, and the noose of Jam was cut. ॥3॥
633.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O man, hold this truth fast in your heart:
the whole world is like a dream; it takes no time at all to perish.
A wall of sand, though raised and plastered with care, does not last four days;
just so are these pleasures of Maya; you fool, why are you caught up (in them)?
Understand even now, nothing is lost yet; worship the Name of Murari.
Says Nanak: I have proclaimed to you aloud the Saadhs' own counsel. ॥2॥
633.2: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
In this world (I) have seen no friend at all.
The whole world is bent on its own comfort; in sorrow (no one) stands by.
Wife, friends, sons and kin are all attached to wealth;
the moment they saw the man penniless, they all left his company and fled.
What am I to say to this crazed mind? It has given its love to these,
and the praise of the Master of the meek, who dispels every fear, it has forgotten.
Like a dog's tail, (it) has not become straight, though I have tried hard.
Says Nanak: (O God,) keep the honour of your age-old way; I have taken your Name. ॥3॥
633.3: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, you have not taken up the Guru's teaching.
What of it, if you have shaved your head and put on saffron robes?
Leaving the True, (man) has clung to the false, and lost his life to no purpose;
by deceit he has fed his own belly, and slept like a beast.
He has not known the way of Ram's worship, and has sold himself into Maya's hands;
the madman has stayed entangled in the pleasures of the senses, and forgotten the jewel of the Naam.
He has stayed heedless, not remembered Gobind, and his span of life has run out in vain.
Says Nanak: O Lord, keep in mind your age-old way; mortals are forever going astray. ॥3॥
633.4: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
The man who in sorrow does not feel sorrow,
who has no fondness for pleasure and no fear, who holds gold as clay;
in whom there is neither slander nor praise, nor greed, attachment and pride;
who stays aloof from joy and grief, (for whom) there is neither honour nor dishonour;
who gives up all hope and desire, and expects nothing of the world;
whom lust and anger do not touch: in his heart Brahm (God) dwells.
The man on whom the Guru has shown grace has recognised this way;
O Nanak, he has merged with Gobind as water merges with water. ॥3॥
634.1: Raag Sorath, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Know this in your mind, dear friend:
the world is bound up in its own comfort alone; no one belongs to anyone.
In good times many come and sit together (with one), and keep (him) surrounded on all four sides;
when hardship falls, all of them leave his company, and no one comes near.
The wife of the house, so dearly loved, who always stays close at his side,
the moment the swan (the soul) left this body, fled from him, crying, pret, pret (a ghost).
Such are the dealings of those to whom (one) has given his love;
at the last moment, O Nanak, no one but the dear Lord has been of any use. ॥3॥
634.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis Chautuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I do not fall into duality, I worship none but the Lord, I go to no tomb or cremation ground.
Caught up in craving, I do not go to another's house; the Naam has quenched (my) craving.
Within the home (of the heart) the Guru has shown (God's) home; it is pleasing to (my) mind, dyed in Sahaj.
You yourself are the Knower, you yourself the Discerner; it is you who give understanding, O Master.
Dyed in bairag (longing for the Lord), the mind has become a bairagi (detached from the world); my mind is pierced by the Shabad, O my mother.
Within is (God's) Light, the Bani through and through, and the mind is attuned to the True Master.
Countless bairagis talk of bairag, (but) he is the bairagi who pleases the Master;
(who), through the Shabad, is steeped in his heart in (God's) fear always, and does the Guru's work;
(who) remembers the One alone, whose mind does not waver, (who) checks it as it runs and holds it still;
(who), rapt in Sahaj, ever dyed in (God's) love, sings the praises of the True One.
If the mind, (restless as) the wind, dwells even a little in the Name, the home of peace, there is peace, O brother;
(his) tongue, eyes and ears are dyed in the True One; the burning (of craving) is put out: (O God,) it is you who have put it out.
The bairagi stays free of hopes, and sits in deep absorption in his own home (within).
Sated with the alms of the Naam, (such ones) are content; in Sahaj they have been given Amrit to drink.
In duality there is no bairag, so long as there is even a mustard-seed of other (hope).
The whole world is yours, you are the one Giver; there is no other, none second, O dear one.
Manmukh creatures dwell in sorrow always; to the Gurmukh (God) gives glory.
(He) is limitless, without end, unreachable, beyond the senses; (his) worth is not found by telling.
(He) abides in Sunn Samadhi, the Lord of the three worlds; (his) Name is the highest good of all.
On the foreheads of beings born into the world is a writ; each one bears the writ upon his own head.
(God) himself has (beings) do their deeds and good deeds; he himself makes devotion firm (in them).
By heeding (God's) fear, the filth of mind and mouth is removed; the Unreachable One himself (grants) wisdom.
Only those who have tasted (it) know its flavour, like the sweet a mute has eaten.
What can be said of the Indescribable, O brother? May I walk ever in (his) Will.
If the Guru unites (one) with the Giver, then understanding comes; one without a Guru has no understanding at all.
As he makes us walk, so we walk, O brother; what other cleverness can anyone try?
Some are led astray in doubt, some are dyed in devotion; your play is boundless.
Whatever you have set (beings) to, such fruit (they) have received; you are the One who moves (all) by your Hukam.
Had I something that was mine, I would serve (you) with it; this soul and body are yours.
On meeting the True Guru, grace has been shown, and the Amrit Name is (my) support.
He who dwells in the inner sky (the highest spiritual realm): in him virtues shine forth, and in virtues are (his) wisdom and meditation.
The Naam is pleasing to (his) mind; he utters it and has (others) utter it, and tells of the Essence of essences alone.
The Shabad of the Guru, the Pir, is deep and profound; without the Shabad the world has gone mad.
O Nanak, the one whose mind accepts the True One is the perfect bairagi, blessed with good fortune, (abiding) in Sahaj. ॥8॥
635.1: Raag Sorath, a Tituki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Hopes and desires are bonds, O brother, and religious rites bring bondage;
through sin and merit the world is born, O brother, and forgetting the Naam it perishes;
this Maya bewitches the world, O brother, and all (such) rites are vain.
Listen, O pandit, you who perform rites:
the deed from which peace springs, O brother, is reflection on the essence of the self.
(The pandit) stands up and recites the Shastra and the Veda, O brother, (but) the deeds you do are worldly;
by hypocrisy the filth does not go, O brother; within is the filth of vice.
In this way the spider perishes, O brother, hanging head down (in its own web).
Through evil understanding many have been ruined, O brother, led astray by the love of another.
Without the True Guru the Naam is not found, O brother, and without the Naam doubt does not go.
If (one) serves the True Guru, then he finds peace, O brother, and his coming and going ends.
Lasting Sahaj springs from the Guru, O brother, and the mind, made pure, merges in the True One.
He who serves the Guru understands, O brother; without the Guru the path is not found.
What do rites avail the one within whom is greed, O brother? Speaking falsehood, he eats poison.
O pandit, when curd is churned, O brother, the essence (butter) comes out of it;
churn water, and water is all one sees, O brother; this world is just such a thing.
Without the Guru one is ruined in doubt, O brother, (though) the unseen Lord is in every heart.
This world is a thread of cotton yarn, O brother, tied by Maya in all ten directions;
without the Guru the knot is not untied, O brother; (people) have grown weary performing rites.
This world is led astray by doubt, O brother; nothing can be said (of it).
On meeting the Guru, the fear (of God) dwells in the mind, O brother; to die in (that) fear is the true writ.
Bathing (at tiraths), charity, good deeds: (yet) in the Lord's court the Naam excels, O brother.
The Guru is the goad (that drives the elephant), who has made the Naam firm (within), O brother; (the Naam) has come to dwell in the mind, and the outward garb is gone.
This body is the Assayer's shop, O brother, and the merchandise is the infinite Naam.
That trader secures this merchandise, O brother, who reflects through the Guru's Shabad.
Blessed, O Nanak, is the trader, O brother, who carries on (this) trade in the company (of the holy). ॥8॥
636.1: Raag Sorath, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who have served the True Guru, beloved: their companions (too) have crossed over.
No bar is put in their way, beloved; on (their) tongue is the Lord's Amrit.
Without (God's) fear, those heavy (with sins) have drowned, beloved; (God) carries (one) across when he casts his glance of grace.
Ever you alone are to be praised, O Beloved; ever, your praise (is to be sung).
Without the ship (of this praise) one drowns in the fearful (ocean), Beloved; where is the shore to be reached?
The Praiseworthy One is to be praised, beloved; there is no other, none second.
Those who praise my God are good, beloved; those dyed in the Shabad are coloured with (his) love.
If one gains the company of such a one, beloved, he tastes the sweet essence and, churning, (reaches) the Essence (God).
Honour is the pass of the True One, beloved, and the Naam is (its) true seal.
Whoever has come must write (this pass) and take it along, beloved; recognise the Hukam of the One who commands.
Without the Guru the Hukam is not understood, beloved; the True One's might stands for ever.
By the Hukam (a being) is conceived, beloved; by the Hukam (it grows) within the womb;
by the Hukam it is born, beloved, upside down, head first.
The Gurmukh is known in the Lord's court, beloved; he departs having set his task right.
By the Hukam (a being) has come, beloved; by the Hukam alone he departs.
By the Hukam he is bound and driven off, beloved; the manmukh receives punishment.
By the Hukam (God) is recognised through the Shabad, beloved, and (one) goes to the Lord's court robed in honour.
By the Hukam accounts are reckoned, beloved; by the Hukam are Haumai and duality.
By the Hukam (a being) wanders and is made to wander, beloved; robbed by its faults, (the world) weeps.
If the Hukam of the Banker (God) is recognised, beloved, the True One is met, and glory comes.
It is said to be hard to utter, beloved; how is the True Name to be heard?
Those who have praised him, beloved: I am a sacrifice to them.
May I gain the Name and be content, beloved; may I be united in union with the Gracious One.
If the body becomes the paper, beloved, and the mind is made the inkpot,
and the tongue the pen of Truth, beloved, then reflect on the Lord's virtues and write them down.
Blessed, O Nanak, is the scribe, beloved, who enshrines the Truth in his heart and writes it. ॥8॥
636.2: Raag Sorath, a Dutuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You are the Giver of virtues, the Pure One, O dear one; (our) mind does not become pure.
We are offenders, without virtue, O dear one; that virtue (comes) from you alone.
O my Beloved, you are the Creator: having made (me), watch over (me).
I am a sinner, a hypocrite, O dear one: (grant that) the Name stand foremost in my mind and body.
The poison of Maya has bewitched the mind, O brother; by cleverness (one) loses honour.
The Master dwells in the mind through Truth, O brother, if the Guru's wisdom sinks in.
Call (him) beautiful, beautiful, O brother: beautiful, a deep crimson.
If the mind longs for the Lord, O brother, then at the door and in the home (of the heart) is the True One, who never errs.
In the underworlds and in the sky are you, O dear one; in every heart are you, (giving) the knowledge of virtues.
On meeting the Guru, peace is found, O brother, and pride has left the mind.
Rub and scour the body with water, O brother, and still the body grows unclean.
Bathe in wisdom, the supreme essence, O brother, and mind and body become pure.
If one worships goddesses and gods, O brother, what am I to ask of them? What can they give?
The stone (idol) is washed with water, O brother, yet such (stones) sink in water.
Without the Guru the Unseen is not seen, O brother; the world drowns, having lost its honour.
Glories are in my Master's hands, O brother; he gives them to whom he pleases.
The bride who speaks sweetly, O brother, and in love of her Husband speaks the Truth,
pierced by the pain of separation, dwells in the True One, O brother, and stays deeply absorbed in the Lord's Name.
Each one calls (God) his own, O brother; (but) through the Guru (one) comes to understand the All-wise One.
Those who are pierced (by love) are saved, O brother; the Shabad is (their) true seal.
Gather a great heap of firewood, O brother, and put in it a spark of fire, (and it all burns away);
(so) if the Naam dwells in the heart even for an instant, O brother, then, O Nanak, union (with God) comes with ease. ॥10॥
637.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, a Tituki, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Dear Lord, you ever protect your devotees; you have been protecting them from the very beginning.
Dear Lord, you saved your servant Prahlad, and destroyed Harnakhash.
The Gurmukhs have faith (in you), dear Lord; the manmukhs are led astray by doubt.
Dear Lord, this (keeping your devotees' honour) is your greatness.
Keep the honour of your devotees, O Master; the devotees are in your refuge.
Jam cannot so much as eye the devotees; death does not go near them.
The Name of Ram alone dwells in their minds; through the Name itself they have found liberation.
All the riddhis and siddhis cling to the feet of the devotees, who (abide) through the Guru in Sahaj and in love.
The manmukhs do not come to have faith; within them is greed and self-interest.
Through the Guru, the Shabad has not pierced their hearts, and they have no love for the Lord's Name.
The veneer of falsehood and deceit will come off; the manmukhs' speech is insipid.
You yourself are at work within your devotees, dear God; it is the devotees who have known you.
The whole world is in attachment to your Maya; you alone are the Being, the Creator.
(Those who) have killed Haumai, and whose desire has merged into the mind itself, have recognised (you) through the Guru's Shabad.
O God, you do the tasks of those who love the Lord's Name, and they are free of care.
By the Guru's grace he ever dwells in their minds, the One who sets all tasks right.
Whoever vies with those who have the Lord God as their protector is ruined.
Without serving the True Guru no one has found (him); the manmukhs have died babbling and wailing.
They come and go and find no resting place; in pain they are absorbed in pain.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh drinks the Amrit, and merges in Sahaj in the True One.
Without serving the True Guru the round of births does not let (one) go, though one perform countless rites in plenty.
(They) read the Vedas and expound disputes; without the Lord they have lost (their) honour.
True is the True Guru, whose Bani is true; those who run to the Guru's refuge are set free.
Those in whose minds the Lord dwells are true at (his) door; at the True door they are found truthful.
Their glory has shone in every age; there is no one who can erase it.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who have kept the Lord enshrined in their hearts. ॥8॥
638.1: Raag Sorath, a Dutuki, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(God) himself forgives those without virtue, O brother, setting them to the service of the True Guru.
The service of the True Guru is sublime, O brother; (through it) the mind is fixed on the Name of Ram.
The dear Lord himself forgives and unites (us with himself).
We are without virtue, and sinners, O brother; the perfect True Guru has taken (us) in among (his own).
So many sinners has he forgiven, O dear one, through reflection on the true Shabad;
he has carried (them) across the terrifying world-ocean, O brother, putting (them) aboard the True Guru's boat.
From burnt iron they have become gold, O brother, as the Guru, the paras, joined them in union (with God).
Once they gave up self, the Name came to dwell in their minds, O brother, and their light was merged into the Light.
I am a sacrifice, I am devoted, O brother; to the True Guru I am ever a sacrifice,
who has given (me) the treasure of the Naam, O brother; through the Guru's teaching I am merged in Sahaj.
Without the Guru Sahaj does not arise, O brother; go and ask those who have wisdom.
Serve the True Guru always, O brother, ridding yourself of self from within.
Through the Guru's teaching the fear (of God) arises, O brother; that fear is the deed to be done, true and sublime.
(Through it) the precious gift of love is found, O brother, and the True Name (becomes one's) support.
Those who serve their True Guru, O brother: I fall at their feet.
(Thus) I make my life worthy, O brother, and win forgiveness for my family as well.
The true (Name), the Bani and the true Shabad, O brother, come by the Guru's grace.
O Nanak, the one in whose mind the Lord's Name dwells, O brother, meets no obstacle at all. ॥8॥
639.1: Raag Sorath, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The dear Lord is known through the Shabad, O brother; by perfect fortune (the Guru) unites (one with him).
The happy soul-brides are ever in peace, O brother; keeping love (for him), night and day they are dyed (in it).
Dear Lord, you yourself dye (the soul) in your love.
Sing, sing (his praises), you who are dyed in his love, O brothers, with your love fixed on the Lord.
She who does the Guru's work, O brother, giving up self and fixing her mind (on it),
has Sahaj forever, and no pain touches her again, O brother; the Lord himself comes to dwell in her mind.
She who does not know her Husband's Hukam, O brother, is an ill-mannered, unworthy wife;
she does her work out of the mind's stubbornness, O brother; without the Name she is false.
They alone sing (his praises) on whose foreheads there is good fortune, O brother; through love of the True One (comes) detachment.
Dyed (in his love), night and day they dwell on his virtues, O brother; free of fear, they hold their attention fixed through the Guru.
He kills all and brings them to life, O brother: serve him day and night.
Why should he be forgotten from the mind, O brother, whose gift is so great?
The self-willed (soul-bride) is filthy and double-minded, O brother; she has no place in the Lord's court.
If she becomes Gurmukh, she dwells on his virtues, O brother, and meeting the Beloved she merges in the True One.
One who has not remembered the Lord in this birth, O brother: what face will he show on going (there)?
Even as the calls (of warning) were sounding, he let himself be robbed, O brother, lured by Maya.
Those who cherish the Name dwell in peace, O brother; their bodies are ever at peace and calm.
Says Nanak, O brother, cherish the Name of the Infinite, the Treasure of virtues, the Profound. ॥8॥
639.2: Raag Sorath, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
He who himself created the whole world, O brother, is the Cause of creation, all-powerful;
he who fashioned the soul and the body, O brother, giving (them) his own power:
by whom can he be told, how can he be seen, O brother? The Creator is One, beyond telling.
Let us praise the Guru, (who is) Govind, O brother, through whom the essence (of all) becomes known.
O my mind, let us repeat (the Name of) the Lord God,
who gives the gift of the Name to his servants, and destroys pain and suffering.
He in whose house is everything, O brother, whose storehouses are full of the nine treasures:
his worth cannot be put, O brother; he is lofty, unreachable and boundless.
He sustains all beings and creatures, O brother, and takes care of them day after day.
Let us meet the perfect True Guru, O brother, who through the Shabad unites (us with him).
Let the feet of the True One be served, O brother; (then) doubt and fear are destroyed.
Joining the gathering of Sants, let the mind be scoured, O brother; (then one) dwells in the Lord's Name.
The darkness of ignorance is dispelled, O brother, and the lotus (of the heart) blossoms.
Through the Guru's words peace wells up, O brother; all fruits are with the True Guru.
Let us give up mine and yours, O brother, and become the dust of all.
God (Brahm) is spread out in every heart, O brother; ever present, he sees and hears.
On the day the Supreme Lord is forgotten, O brother, on that day one dies in grief.
He is all-powerful, and does and causes all to be done, O brother; he is full of every power.
The Name is the precious gift of love, O brother, the end of attachment to Maya.
When it pleases him he unites (one with himself), O brother, and the Name dwells in the heart.
Through the Guru the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, O brother, and light dawns in the heart.
God's glory has become manifest, O brother; earth and sky are in bloom.
(The one whom) the perfect Guru has made content, O brother, is attached in love (to God) day and night.
With his tongue he ever dwells on Ram, O brother; (this is his) true relish and aim.
Hearing (the praises) with his ears again and again he lives, O brother; he has found the unmoving place.
One to whom faith does not come, O brother: may that wretched soul burn!
My Master has many virtues, O brother; I am a sacrifice to him.
He cherishes the worthless, O brother, and gives a place to the placeless.
He provides sustenance with every breath, O brother, he whose Name is of a deep colour.
The one who meets the True Guru, O brother, has perfect fortune.
Without him one cannot live for a moment, O brother; he is full of every power.
With no breath or morsel is he forgotten, O brother; I see him ever present.
In the Saadh's company (he) has united (me with himself), O brother, the One who fills all.
Those in whom love (for him) has not arisen, O brother, die in grief day after day.
Attaching (me) to the hem of his robe, he has carried (me) across the terrifying ocean, O brother, the world of pain.
In his grace he has looked on (me) with his glance, O brother; he has taken (my) side beyond measure.
Mind and body have become cool, O brother; the Name is (my) food and support.
Nanak (has come to) the refuge of him, O brother, who cuts away sins. ॥9॥
640.1: Raag Sorath, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mother's womb is an ocean of pain, O dear one; there (God) had (the being) repeat his own Name.
Once (he) brought (it) out, the poison (of Maya) spread, O dear one, and (he) made attachment to Maya grow.
The one on whom (God) himself has shown his grace, O dear one, he has united with the perfect Guru.
That one worships (God) with every breath, O dear one, with attention fixed on the Name of Ram.
In (my) mind and body is your support, O Beloved; in (my) mind and body is your support.
There is no doer but you, O Beloved; you are the One, the Inner-knower.
Having wandered through millions of births, (the being) has come (here), O dear one, suffering pain in countless species.
(Here) the True Master is forgotten, O dear one, and great punishment is received.
Those whom the perfect True Guru meets, O dear one, are attached to the True Name.
Following those who are in the true refuge, O dear one, one is set free.
What (one) ate taking it for sweet, O dear one, has brought disease into the body.
It turned bitter and settled in, O dear one; from it grief has sprung.
Feeding (beings) on pleasures, (God) has led (them) astray, O dear one; (their) separation does not end.
Those whom (God) has saved by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, had their union ordained from the very Source.
In one steeped in greed for Maya, O Beloved, you never come into the mind at all.
Those who forget you, O Supreme Lord, O Master, their bodies have turned to dust.
They wail a great deal, O dear one, (but their) agony does not leave.
Those whom (God) has set right by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, their capital is kept safe.
Do not keep company with a Saakat, O dear one, as far as it lies in your power,
meeting whom the Lord is forgotten, O dear one; such a one rises and departs with a blackened face.
The manmukh finds no shelter, O dear one; in the Lord's court he receives punishment.
Those whom (God) has set right by uniting them with the Guru, O dear one, succeed in full.
A thousand disciplines and clevernesses, O dear one: not one has gone along (with anyone).
Those who turn their faces from Gobind, O dear one, bring a stain upon their family.
(They) have not known the thing that is (theirs, within), O dear one; falsehood has not gone along (with anyone).
Those whom (God) has united with the True Guru, O dear one, cherish the True Name.
Truth, contentment, wisdom and meditation, O dear one, (come to the one) on whom (God) casts his glance of grace.
Night and day he sings his praises and dwells on his virtues, O dear one, filled to the brim with Amrit.
They have crossed the ocean of pain, O dear one; they have gone across the terrifying world-ocean.
Whoever is pleasing to you, you unite with yourself, O Beloved; they alone are ever genuine.
God is the all-powerful Being, the merciful Lord, O dear one; the devotees lean on his strength.
(The devotees) have fallen into the refuge, O dear one, of him who is the Inner-knower, the wise.
(He) has set right this world and the next for them, O dear one; on their foreheads is the true mark.
May that God never be forgotten, O dear one; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥8॥
641.1: Raag Sorath, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
One has read the holy texts and pondered the Vedas, and practised nivli and bhuangam;
(yet) the company of the five has not left, and (such people) are bound all the more by a proud intellect.
O dear one, (the Lord) cannot be met in these ways; I have done many (such) deeds.
Defeated, I have fallen at the Master's door: (O Master,) give (me) an intellect that discerns.
One has kept silence, lived as a karpati, and wandered naked in the forest;
one has roamed the river banks, the tiraths and all the earth; (but) duality does not leave.
Driven by the mind's desire, one has gone to live at a tirath, and had the saw put to the head;
but the mind's filth does not go in this way, though one make a hundred thousand efforts.
Gold, women, fine horses and elephants: one gives gifts of many kinds;
one offers grain, clothes and land in plenty; (yet) one does not reach the Lord's door.
One stays absorbed in worship, the worship of images, bowing, prostrating and the six rites;
(but) saying I, I, one falls into bonds; (the Lord) is not met by this method.
The yoga of the Siddhs, the eighty-four postures: one has done these too, over and over, till weary.
Living to a great age, one is born again and again, (for one) has not grasped union with the Lord.
Royal pleasures, the pomp of kings, issuing commands none can refuse,
a beautiful bed, sandal and perfume: (these are) the gate of terrible hell.
The Lord's praise in the Saadh Sangat is the deed above all deeds.
Says Nanak, it has come to the one whose due was written from before.
Your servant is intoxicated with this love.
The destroyer of the pains of the poor has shown mercy; this mind is dyed in the Kirtan of the Lord, Har Har. ॥1॥
